stories.Headline: AI agents threaten Naver and Kakao as their share prices fall to 2019 levels
stories.Summary:
Naver closed at 156,100 won and Kakao at 30,350 won on the stock market on the 24th, according to The Kyunghyang Shinmun. Both share prices edged up from the previous day's year-to-date lows but were pushed back to levels last seen in November 2019, seven years earlier. The article reported that both companies posted record-high revenue while their share prices kept falling. It said their scale has steadily expanded but the market's appraisal has moved in the opposite direction. The article said growing analysis holds that artificial intelligence is shaking the platform success formula that drove the two companies' growth over the past decade or so.

The article said third-quarter revenue and operating profit both more than doubled over the same period. It said price-to-earnings ratios based on next year's expected results are now 11 times for Naver and 14 times for Kakao, down from 41 times and 32 times seven years earlier. It said total time spent on domestic ChatGPT apps surged 114% in October from a year earlier. It said Naver's advertising revenue growth slowed from 9.3% in the first quarter to 5.5% in the third quarter. It said a McKinsey survey across 11 countries last month found 56% used general-purpose AI search or chatbots for shopping, against 27% for retailers' own AI.

The article said Naver amassed tens of millions of users through search and Kakao through its messenger service, then expanded into advertising and shopping. It said Junho Lee, an analyst at Hana Securities, wrote in a report that day that AI agents would establish themselves as a platform on top of platforms and reshape the existing market order. It said he said those unable to build their own AI agents may end up confined to paying fees to external AIs. It said Minsoo Shin, a professor in the Department of Business Administration at Hanyang University, said changes in the platform market do not happen gradually and cited NateOn users flocking to KakaoTalk all at once. It said he said Naver and Kakao's user bases are assets for now but network effects can disappear quickly once a new platform reaches a tipping point.

The article said Hyojin Lee, an analyst at Meritz Securities, analyzed in a recent report that with generative AI computation costs surge with usage, making it harder to turn a profit than with traditional platforms. It said Kyoungjeon Lee, a professor in the Department of Big Data Analytics at Kyung Hee University, said incumbents have abundant resources for new technologies but face the dilemma of eating into their own earnings. It said he said Naver and Kakao themselves grew by pushing aside former leaders during the transitions to the internet and to smartphones and now face the transition to AI. It said Kakao plans to release its own AI but cannot be complacent. It said Meta's Muse handles everything from product search to payment and the AI assistant Pickle calls restaurants to make reservations.

The article said the more Naver pushes AI search to the fore, the more the position of its traditional search advertising narrows. It said Kakao may see its conventional model of spreading traffic across its services to monetize weaken if AI performs tasks on users' behalf. It said the cost equation of legacy platforms, where margins expanded as users increased, no longer holds. It said the more AI substitutes for search, the greater the potential hit to advertising and shopping businesses, while noting causality cannot be asserted. It said simply adding AI does not guarantee the competitiveness of existing platforms.

The article said it has also become difficult to guarantee platform dominance solely by having a large user base. It said Kakao faces new competition with the emergence of AI agents that select products and even make reservations on behalf of users. It said the market's growth expectations for the two companies have fallen accordingly, reflecting an assessment that their established growth paths have hit a ceiling. It said controlling the daily gateways people pass through is the secret that let the two companies reign as platform behemoths for more than a decade. It did not say what steps either company will take next or when Kakao's own AI will be released.

Articles.Title: Record-high revenue, share prices back to seven years ago… In the AI era, Naver and Kakao's ‘platform success formula’ faces a crisis

stories.Headline: Gaon Cable raises 2027 US sales target 33 percent on AI data center demand
stories.Summary:
Gaon Cable raised the 2027 sales target for its US subsidiary LSCUS by 33.3 percent to 2 trillion won, or about $1.5 billion, on Nov. 24, 2026, according to a Korea Herald report, citing faster than expected orders from AI data centers. LSCUS is expected to post 870 billion won in sales this year, nearly double last year’s 440 billion won, and its 2027 target is about 4.5 times its 2025 sales. Busducts for AI data centers are driving the growth, and LSCUS has secured long-term supply contracts worth more than 5 trillion won with US tech giants through 2030. Under a three-year contract worth about 500 billion won signed with a US tech giant last year, LSCUS had received 330 billion won in purchase orders as of November, which the article says accounted for 66 percent of the expected supply value over the full three-year term.

The company also signed a contract in the first half of this year with another US tech giant for supplies expected to total about 4 trillion won over the next five years. Gaon Cable expects LSCUS’s 2027 sales to comprise 1.3 trillion won in busducts and 700 billion won in distribution cables. To meet rising demand, Gaon Cable plans to double distribution cable capacity at its Tarboro plant in North Carolina by 2027 from end-2025 levels, and it will also expand busduct production through LS Cable’s Gumi plant and a facility in Mexico. The article does not name who at Gaon Cable is responsible for the target or give any statement from the company about it.

Gaon Cable posted record third-quarter revenue of 986.5 billion won and operating profit of 52 billion won, up 51.9 percent and 99.1 percent year on year, respectively. Its operating margin reached 5.3 percent, topping 5 percent for the first time, the article says. The company was also selected for inclusion in both the KOSPI 200 and KRX 300 indices in the Korea Exchange’s second-half index rebalancing, making it the only industrial stock added to both indices, according to the article. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the capacity plans and the 2027 target.

Articles.Title: Gaon Cable lifts US sales target by over 30% amid AI boom

stories.Headline: Korea plans five-year maximum prison term for national technical exam cheating
stories.Summary:
Recent scandals involving hidden cameras and artificial intelligence have renewed calls for tougher laws in Korea. A group used miniature cameras in buttons and neckties to film exam questions dozens of times. The Seoul Central District Court sentenced an education company operator to one year in prison last May. Two colleagues received ten months in prison, while other acquaintances involved in the scheme were fined. This group conspired from October 2021 to April 2023 to sell reconstructed questions to test-takers.

The group targeted 43 exams from 10 public institutions, including Seoul Metro and Korea Railroad Corporation. These test sites were located across the country, including Busan, Daejeon, and the greater Seoul area. The scheme ended in February 2023 at a Gwanak District site after proctors noticed awkward sitting. The operator was convicted of violating the National Technical Qualifications Act and the Copyright Act. The government now plans to increase the maximum prison sentence for national technical exams to five years.

The Seoul Central District Court stated that these crimes undermined the fairness and credibility of national exams. Lawyer Kwak Joon-ho said that public concern over fairness has grown as cheating combines with technology. He noted that the top tax accountant scorer, Han, may receive a light sentence for cooperating. Kwak argued that penalties should be severe now because AI and other technology have changed the outcome. The court explained that the defendants caused considerable disruption to the operation of the national qualification exams.

Critics say that penalties for cheating remain lenient even as sophisticated AI and smart device use spreads. Most cases end in fines or suspended sentences because no general law punishes exam cheating specifically. A test-taker received a six-month suspended sentence in September for using AI on an English test. The top tax accountant scorer, Han, admitted to cheating and was questioned by the police. Lee Jin-woo, who earned a perfect score on the Legal Education Eligibility Test, also faced allegations.

Cases are typically brought under charges of obstruction of business or violating the Copyright Act. Obstruction charges are used because cheaters interfere with the work of assessing candidates for the exams. AI cheating currently carries no separate penalty and draws punishment similar to that for ordinary cheating. Lee Jin-woo was accused of cheating on the College Scholastic Ability Test and the eligibility test. He was found dead on Thursday after failing to appear for a planned livestream event.

The government will introduce legal penalties for cheating on national professional exams to combat AI-assisted cheating. Authorities are currently investigating the methods used by the top scorer of the tax accountant certification exam. The government intends to raise the maximum prison term for technical exam cheating from two to five years. The articles do not state when these new legal penalties for professional exams will be implemented. It remains open whether the new laws will successfully deter the spread of AI exam cheating.

stories.Headline: Samsung promotes 131 staff in 2027 reshuffle to back AI, robotics and foundry experts
stories.Summary:
Samsung Electronics promoted 131 employees during its annual executive reshuffle for 2027, which the company announced on Tuesday, November 24, 2026. This move followed record earnings in the semiconductor division and prioritized experts in artificial intelligence, robotics, and foundry services. The total number of promotions decreased by 18.6 percent, or 30 people, compared to the 161 promotions made in the previous year. The reshuffle included 39 executive vice presidents, 78 vice presidents, 12 masters, and two fellows.

High bandwidth memory experts Ha Kyung-soo, Park Tae-hoon, and Park Jin-pyo were elevated to executive vice president, while Kim Myeong-o and Jang Se-jeong received the same rank for their work on DRAM and solid-state drives. In the foundry business, Song Tae-joong, Lee Ho, and Ryu Hyo-gyeom became executive vice presidents, and Lee Ki-jo was promoted to vice president. Robotics and AI leaders including Koo Dong-han and Hyung Seung-yong became vice presidents, while Mathieu Apotheker was promoted to executive vice president. Additionally, 11 women were promoted, including Lee Yoon-kyong, who attained the rank of executive vice president.

The company stated that it prioritized personnel with proven track records and technology experts who can drive future growth. These appointments reflect a commitment to strengthening future businesses through both internal development and the acquisition of external companies. This process follows a leadership change where Hwang Sang-joon, Cho Sang-yeun, and Lee Jong-myeong were named presidents in the semiconductor division. Vice Chairman Jun Young-hyun and President Roh Tae-moon remain as dual CEOs, but they handed over their roles as heads of the Memory and Mobile eXperience businesses.

The new structure allows Vice Chairman Jun to focus on the foundry business while President Roh concentrates on growth areas like robotics. This reshuffle is intended to provide the technological leadership necessary to support the broader business restructuring. Samsung has now completed its executive appointments for the year. The company plans to finalize and announce its organizational restructuring and executive assignments in the near future.

stories.Headline: TEPS test-takers wear disposable gowns and aprons from December to curb AI cheating
stories.Summary:
Test-takers sitting the TEPS English proficiency exam will have to wear disposable gowns and aprons from next month, amid growing concerns over AI-assisted cheating on exams. TEPS, the Test of English Proficiency developed by Seoul National University, is widely used for university admissions and job applications in Korea. According to the TEPS Council at Seoul National University on Tuesday, candidates will be given the gowns and aprons to wear starting with the 413th regular test on Dec. 5. The council has already banned hats and introduced metal detectors at each test site, starting with a regular test held on Saturday.

Using artificial intelligence, or using or wearing a smart device during the test, will be treated as cheating. Offenders will lose their eligibility for the test and may face legal action. A council official said the measures are intended to protect test-takers and to detect cheating, and that preparations are complete, including the purchase of the supplies. The report was published on Nov. 24, 2026.

More to follow.

stories.Headline: Kyunghyang Shinmun requires 2027 contest entrants to disclose AI use and verify creative process
stories.Summary:
Earlier this month, Kyunghyang Shinmun issued its call for entries for the 2027 New Year Literary Contest and included wording requiring entrants to state whether they used AI. The notice asks entrants who used AI during the writing process to specify the tools used and the purpose and scope of use in detail. Entrants who did not use AI must mark it as "Not used" when submitting, according to the notice. The judging panel may request a phone interview or additional materials for shortlisted entries to verify the creative process and any AI use. If it is confirmed that an entrant deliberately omitted the fact of AI use or falsely stated the scope of use, the award may be canceled.

The core principle of the Kyunghyang Shinmun New Year Literary Contest, that it evaluates works written by humans and selects the outstanding among them, remains unchanged. This year an AI-related notice was prepared for the first time, given that generative AI has become commonplace and is widely used in writing as an auxiliary means such as for research. Marking its 79th iteration, the contest has also changed its submission method to online only starting this year. To improve convenience and fairness in receiving and sorting manuscripts, submissions by mail or in person will not be accepted. Online submissions are open until December 4, and application instructions can be checked online.

One novelist who served as a judge for last year's Kyunghyang Shinmun New Year Literary Contest said about adding a ban on AI that it should go without saying that you must not use AI. The novelist said it is strange to warn people not to do what is obvious. Novelist Hwang Sok-young said earlier this year that he uses AI as an aid to writing. Novelist Moon Ji-hyeok said you cannot punish someone for driving with navigation on, but asked whether we should not at least distinguish whether a human really drove or a machine did. Moon added that going forward, pure literature contests may remain as "small-scale artistic arenas" among those who can generate text on their own and those who can discern it.

Publishing critic Kim Sung-shin said it appears to symbolically show that the side effects of AI confronting literature and publishing have become visible. Kim said that with the government placing emphasis on promoting AI technology, publishing and literature are collapsing badly, and the lack of protection for them is also a problem. Kim added that it is meaningful that authors and rights holders are facing up to these issues and trying to find solutions. The literary world calls it "a symbolic incident that makes AI side effects visible." For last year's Kyunghyang Shinmun New Year Literary Contest, submissions increased over the previous year by 2,289 in poetry and 132 in fiction.

Notices banning AI use began appearing in Korean literary contests around 2023, when AI's capabilities in writing advanced rapidly after the release of ChatGPT in November 2022. Some newspapers that host New Year Literary Contests and publishers that run literary prizes added brief warnings stating that if AI use in a work is confirmed, the award may be revoked. This year, the French Goncourt Prize excluded Telisson Aurelien's from the final shortlist after allegations arose that AI wrote it, even though it had made the first-round list. The Canadian publisher that released the book also said it had confirmed indications of AI use and terminated its contract with Aurelien. In one domestic literary competition as well, a work suspected of using AI made it to the final screening, and after deliberation the judges concluded the prize with "no winner."

Munhakgwa Jiseongsa, which had not included AI-related rules in its rookie contests, plans to add language containing AI use guidelines starting next year. Changbi has stated since last year that "works produced by AI cannot be submitted." Most organizers of this year's New Year Literary Contests added wording to their calls stating that judges may verify, through interviews and other means, the creative process and any AI use for shortlisted works. This year, after Anthropic, developer of the generative AI Claude, was reported to have illegally downloaded digital copies of books by well-known authors at home and abroad, including Han Kang, awareness also grew of the problem of using results produced by AI that trained unlawfully on existing works. The announcement for the 1st Kyunghyang Shinmun New Year Literary Contest was made in 1946.

stories.Headline: South Korea files criminal complaints against five students over AI cheating in national exams
stories.Summary:
Cases of cheating using advanced artificial intelligence tools surfaced in qualification exams and the College Scholastic Ability Test around November 2026. Authorities issued several emergency disaster alerts to trigger audible alarms on banned smartphones during the examinations to stop these activities. The government is now filing criminal complaints against five students who were accused of using devices during the College Scholastic Ability Test. These incidents have caused widespread fear that AI cheating is spreading into university essay exams as well.

The government plans to combat this trend by increasing the maximum prison sentence for cheating on national technical exams from two years to five years. New legal penalties will also be introduced for those who cheat on national professional exams to ensure stricter enforcement. These changes aim to protect the promise that abilities developed through diligent effort will be evaluated fairly. Such measures are intended to prevent dishonest individuals from gaining an unfair advantage over those who follow the rules.

Choi Hoon, a professor of psychology at Hallym University, stated that AI cheating carries serious social consequences for the public. He explained that people feel betrayed when a psychological contract is broken and dishonest success goes unchecked. According to Choi, individuals may stop valuing rules or lose their belief in social fairness if honesty is not rewarded. He argued that society must ensure that those who lead honest and hard working lives are not betrayed.

The author suggests that this crisis reflects a wider social issue where honest work increasingly feels unrewarded in many areas of life. He noted that simply attending classes is often not enough to secure a job in the current competitive environment. This situation may lead people to live like gamblers who hope for one big break rather than relying on steady effort. The rise of these tools threatens the traditional belief that people can shape their lives through their own abilities.

Articles.Title: AI cheating threatens the promise of honest effort

stories.headline_source: AI cheating threatens the promise of honest effort

stories.Headline: Kyung Hee professor Kim Sang-kyun urges teachers to ask questions and foster student judgment in the AI era
stories.Summary:
Kim Sang-kyun, a professor at Kyung Hee University's Graduate School of Business, wrote the column published on November 24, 2026, about AI use in classrooms. He wrote that AI-assisted cheating has shocked society and that students using AI to write book reports have become commonplace in schools. He said their assignments may appear authentic, but closer reading often reveals strange details absent from the books. He said that when asked whether they read the books and wrote the reports themselves, most students protest their innocence. He said adults face a dilemma over whether children should be prohibited from using AI or allowed to use it freely.

The column cites a 2025 experiment published by MIT Media Lab that compared groups writing four essays, some using AI and others working without it. It says brain connectivity was significantly weaker among AI users. It says 83 percent of the AI users reportedly gave incorrect answers when questioned about their essays. It says Samsung Electronics announced on Nov. 17 that it will introduce hands-on sessions featuring its Galaxy XR extended reality headset as part of its Galaxy AI Class educational program. It says students participate in a Galaxy AI Class session using Galaxy XR headsets at Daebang Middle School in Seoul.

Kim said the question is not whether children should use AI but whether they understand it properly. He said generative AI frequently produces incorrect answers with remarkable confidence, a phenomenon known as hallucination, and children may mistake these confident responses for facts. He said understanding AI's limitations and learning to use it responsibly remain fundamentally human responsibilities. He said teachers must become people who ask questions in return, asking students which part reflects their own thinking, how to verify an answer and what AI has overlooked. He said students should spend at least five minutes thinking independently before using AI for homework and should close their screens and rewrite their work in their own words afterward.

Kim said he calls the phenomenon of middle school students treating AI like a friend "artificial relationships." He said children confide worries to AI that they hesitate to share with friends or teachers. He said adults should ask, from the child's perspective, whether after talking with AI the child wants to spend more time with friends or less. He said he recently delivered a special lecture at a teacher training program organized by the CJ Welfare Foundation through its CJ Donors Camp initiative for teachers working in child welfare facilities. He said some children were already proficient AI users while others had encountered the technology for the first time at community child centers.

Kim said every technological advance, from calculators and the internet to smartphones, has provoked anxiety, and older generations have always worried about new technologies, but humanity has adapted. He said AI can create the illusion of intellectual effort because it produces finished work, and repeated dependence risks weakening children's capacity for inquiry. He said the traditional role of teachers as providers of correct answers is diminishing because children increasingly turn to AI first when they have questions. He said relationships among peers inevitably involve friction, making an AI companion that consistently takes their side particularly appealing, but people develop closer relationships by resolving conflicts. He said the program sought to strengthen the capabilities of teachers working in child welfare facilities, and together they considered what education should look like in the AI era.

Kim said teachers who patiently ask questions, examine answers alongside children and give them time to develop their own ideas create lasting educational experiences. He said children need adults who think alongside them rather than simply supply correct answers in the AI era. He said teachers should cultivate curiosity, judgment and confidence, not merely supervise technology use. He said children who learn to reason through problems with others will eventually become adults capable of cooperating, resolving differences and building a better society together. The column does not say what specific policies schools should adopt or how AI use in classrooms will be regulated.

stories.Headline: Seoul medical students post video solving Suneung Korean section
stories.Summary:
Three first-year medical students at Seoul National University posted a YouTube video in which they worked through the Korean language section of this year's Suneung, the national college entrance exam held on Thursday, and then shared their results along with footage of how each reached their answers. Two of the three entered the medical school through early admissions and the third through regular admissions, and one of them said in the video that none of them had known about AI glasses or such cheating methods during the admissions process, let alone used them. Lee Jin-woo, a first-year dentistry student at Seoul National University who scored perfectly on this year's Legal Education Eligibility Test, had pledged to take the Korean language section on a livestream, and he was found dead in an apparent suicide on Thursday, hours after he failed to show up for the demonstration he had proposed in response to the cheating allegations. On Nov. 12, the second-highest scorer on this year's tax accountant qualification exam posted a YouTube video of themselves solving questions from the tax accounting section, extending the trend beyond the Suneung.

The trend follows a series of high-profile cases of AI-assisted cheating that have fueled growing distrust of academic achievements and professional credentials. The Ministry of Education announced that 111 cases of cheating involving electronic devices were detected during Thursday's Suneung, and five of those involved devices such as smart glasses and miniature cameras. On Nov. 15, Han Won-seok, 34, who ranked first in both stages of this year's tax accountant exam, admitted to obtaining answers with the help of a miniature camera, a generative AI model and a smartphone. Han, who correctly answered 159 of 160 questions in the first round, also confessed to using the same method in the first stage of the certified public accountant exam in March, which he failed.

Investigators at the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency have searched Han's residence and secured digital forensic evidence as part of their ongoing investigation, and he underwent his fourth round of police questioning on Monday. Han reportedly photographed test questions with a camera attached to a correction tape dispenser and used a modified calculator to relay the images to a laptop at his home via a smartphone hidden inside an abdominal support belt. He then viewed the AI-generated responses on a miniature monitor concealed on his body. The articles do not say what further action is planned in the investigation or what consequences the students and professionals who posted the videos may face.

Articles.Title: No AI needed: Exam high-flyers put their skills on display

stories.Headline: Korea plans tougher CSAT rules after more than 100 test takers are caught with smart devices
stories.Summary:
More than 100 test takers were caught with smart devices during the CSAT, The Korea Times reported, despite repeated warnings and measures against AI-enabled cheating from authorities. The exam was held on Nov. 18, and test takers entered CSAT sites at high schools including one in Yongsan District, Seoul. A student cried in her mother's arms after finishing the test at a high school in Gangwon Province the same day. The government will now spend a year preparing tougher policies for next year's exam. The article was published Nov. 25, 2026, by Park Ung.

In 2025, 58.2 percent of Koreans aged 25 to 64 had completed higher education, compared with the OECD average of 42.6 percent, according to Ministry of Education data released in September. Among those aged 25 to 34, the figure was 71.1 percent, the highest of any OECD member country, and Korea has led the OECD in higher education attainment among young adults for 18 consecutive years. People aged 15 to 29 took an average of 11.3 months to find their first job in 2025, according to the Korea Enterprises Federation, with those holding a high school education or less taking 16.5 months and those with a college degree or higher taking 8.8 months. High school and junior college graduates in their third year out of high school earned an average of about 1.67 million won a month, according to a 2025 Korean Educational Development Institute report, while Ministry of Employment and Labor data show workers aged 20 to 24 earned about 2.65 million won a month in 2024, roughly 59 percent more. A 2022 survey commissioned by the Educational Broadcasting System polled 2,798 people in their 20s, including about 550 each in Korea, the United States, Germany, Japan and Denmark.

The government planned the tougher policies after the more than 100 test takers were caught with smart devices on the CSAT. The article's author, Park Ung, wrote that he never took the CSAT and skipped it to travel the world, working as a cleaner in Australia for a year and touring 24 countries in another year. He wrote that he applied two years in a row only to the Korea National University of Arts, one of the country's most coveted arts schools, even though a single rejection meant no college at all. He wrote that he treated college as a trophy when his own turn came. He wrote that no matter how strong the countermeasures, some will still try to cheat unless Korean society lets go of its deep-rooted belief that you have to go to college, and a good one at that.

In the 2022 survey, 42.3 percent of Korean respondents in their 20s said people cannot be respected in life if they do poorly in school, the highest share among the five countries, compared with 37.6 percent in Japan, 24.9 percent in Germany, 22.2 percent in the U.S. and 20 percent in Denmark. In Korea, 60.4 percent said the purpose of studying through high school was to get into a good college, while 21.3 percent said high school was as far as they hoped to go, the lowest share among all the countries and roughly half the 41.3 percent in the U.S. and 40.3 percent in Germany. The top answer in the U.S. was discovering one's aptitudes, interests and potential, at 31.5 percent, and in Denmark it was gaining knowledge needed in everyday life, at 31.8 percent. In an open-ended question asking what it means to fail in life, many in Korea pointed to falling short in college admissions or job hunting, the researchers said, while those in Denmark gave answers such as committing a crime. The survey covered Korea, the United States, Germany, Japan and Denmark.

The article said Korea's strong emphasis on college admission shapes young people's education and career choices, with consequences for job prospects and social perceptions. It said Korean society pushes people hard to go to college, and not just any college but a good one. It said high school graduates are at a disadvantage on every front in the job market. It said the divide between high school and college graduates goes beyond the numbers to social perceptions. It said the author, in his early 30s, would give the same advice to go to college to someone younger in a similar situation who plans to live in Korea.

The government will spend a year preparing tougher policies for next year's exam. The article said crackdowns alone can hardly stop AI cheating if college serves as trophy rather than education. It said some will still try to cheat unless Korean society lets go of its belief that you have to go to college. It did not say what the tougher policies would contain. It did not say what penalties the more than 100 test takers caught with smart devices face.

stories.Headline: Education founder Dmytro Korchevskyi proposes four assignment design methods to stop students offloading thinking to AI
stories.Summary:
Dmytro Korchevskyi wrote an opinion piece on November 25, 2026, about preventing students from offloading their thinking to artificial intelligence. He developed four specific approaches to assignment design with his curriculum team for a network of schools he founded. These methods aim to ensure students do the bulk of intellectual work even when AI answers are available. The author believes that banning the use of AI is not the correct solution for modern education. He argues that only a person can spark a student's interest, whereas a machine can only suggest things.

The first approach involves placing the student inside the story by framing lesson topics around the student as the protagonist. Teachers can ask students to imagine being in Caesar's shoes to force them to work out the situation. The second method adds oral presentations to assignments so students must explain their conclusions and reasoning aloud to teachers. The third approach replaces simple practice programs with the creation of working prototypes, such as a video service with features. Finally, teachers can set many short micro-tasks during a lesson that are too fiddly to delegate to AI.

Dmytro Korchevskyi, a doctor of pedagogical sciences, is the founder of STEP IT Academy and a network of schools in Ukraine. He stated that real learning takes place during discussions and presentations when students link facts and arguments from memory. He noted that students who work through material independently answer questions with ease compared to those reading generated text. Korchevskyi believes that basic skills remain important because they allow students to bring their own creative ideas to fruition. He claims that micro-tasks prevent students from disengaging from the learning process by requiring modest independent intellectual effort.

A Pew Research Center survey of students aged 13 to 17 found one in ten American teenagers use AI chatbots. This survey indicates that these students complete all or most of their schoolwork with the help of such tools. A separate study of nearly 300 teachers conducted two years ago found staff identified AI essays in only 37.8 percent. This suggests that AI output is often so convincing that teachers cannot always distinguish it from work written by humans. Students can now easily tailor their answers to the required tone and format using the latest AI models.

The author began his career giving private programming lessons as a student before opening his first training center in 1999. He personally wrote the first curricula and trained the first instructors for his educational ventures in the IT field. His academy now operates as a global network that provides IT education across 26 different countries around the world. He observes that students are more likely to study a subject if it helps them achieve a personal goal. This background informs his view that assignments must be structured to encourage active thinking rather than mere formality.

The proposed methods allow AI to be used for gathering material or drawing up a plan for a task. Teachers can use tricky questions during oral defenses to see if students understand the work they have submitted. The author suggests that students can use AI to produce a first version of a product more quickly. The articles do not state if these four approaches have been tested across all 26 countries of the academy. It remains open whether these specific design changes can fully stop students from offloading their thinking to machines.

stories.Headline: CMC launches Clex AI legal platform for government agencies and businesses
stories.Summary:
On November 25th, in Hanoi, CMC Technology Group officially launched Clex, a Make in Vietnam artificial intelligence legal platform for government agencies and businesses, with the message “Mastering the law ,  Creating civilization”. Deputy Prime Minister Ho Quoc Dung attended the launch ceremony. Delegates at the event experienced Clex's outstanding features. The development team demonstrated its ability to search and extract legal knowledge, support document processing and review, and cite legal grounds for users to verify results. The demo gave guests a more visual understanding of how AI can support professional work, from government agencies to corporate governance and legal compliance.

Clex was researched and developed by CMC on the basis of a large-scale language model specializing in Vietnamese law, trained and refined on a knowledge base of over 2 million legal documents. Clex comprises two product lines: Clex GOV for government agencies and Clex ENTERPRISE for businesses. For government agencies, the platform supports searching, compiling, drafting, comparing, reviewing conflicts and overlaps, and assessing documents, and assists officials in advising, processing files, and handling administrative procedures. For businesses, Clex integrates internal documents, supports legal research, contract review, policy change monitoring, impact assessment, and compliance obligation identification. As of November 20, 2026, the shared AI platform supporting public service, including Clex and AI Law, is providing hundreds of thousands of active accounts across 17 central government agencies at the ministerial level and all 34 provinces and cities nationwide.

Deputy Minister of Science and Technology Tran Trung Tinh highly appreciated the approach to deploying AI platforms to support public service by mobilizing resources from businesses, instead of the State investing in construction or appointing a development unit. He said the Ministry of Science and Technology has announced a set of criteria and established an evaluation council of 31 members representing four ministries and agencies, as well as experts. He said businesses proactively register, and products are put into use based on meeting the evaluation criteria. He said this approach contributes to saving budget, limiting duplicate investments, and promoting domestic technological capabilities. He said in the long term CMC needs to continue investing in its research team and cooperating with legal experts to improve product quality, and that the success of Clex should be evaluated by its practical application effectiveness, its ability to support officials, and the specific values it brings to the performance of official duties.

Mr. Dang Van Tu, General Director of CMC AIX, emphasized that Clex is built on an understanding of three core elements: users, the legal system, and technology. He said that during the AI training process for officials in the Government Office, ministries, departments, and local government at the ward and commune levels, CMC had the opportunity to understand the practical challenges faced by users. He said these challenges include the need to quickly find applicable regulations, identify currently valid documents, detect policy changes, and have a clear legal basis for handling work. He introduced the journey of applying Clex through five values: Understanding, Perceiving, Understanding, Convenience, and Advantage. He said “Convenience” involves integrating Clex into familiar work tools such as Microsoft Word, Hanoiwork in Hanoi, and the software systems currently used in Hai Phong.

Mr. Nguyen Trung Chinh, Chairman of the Board and Executive Chairman of CMC Technology Group, emphasized that CMC is committed to continuing to invest in and master technology, constantly improving Clex in a way that is accurate, reliable, safe, accessible, and centered around the people and users. He said the Group aims to bring the platform to every official and civil servant to improve the efficiency of serving the people, and to support the business community in reducing compliance costs and enhancing governance capacity. He said it also helps every citizen access, understand, and enforce the law more conveniently and equally. He said CMC will proactively coordinate with state management agencies, research institutions, and the business community to further improve the product and create practical value. He said Clex is not only a Vietnamese intellectual product but also reflects the aspiration to master technology, develop solutions that serve the interests of people, businesses, and the community, and contribute to the development of the country.

Through the evaluation, two platforms met the requirements, including Clex, both developed by Vietnamese businesses and deployed on infrastructure in Vietnam. Clex was selected by the Ministry of Science and Technology as a pilot AI platform to support public service, and was chosen by the Ministry of Justice to participate in the comprehensive review program of legal documents and to be uploaded to the National Legal Portal. CMC developed large language models and visual-linguistic models specifically for Vietnamese law, trained and validated on the V-LegalBench assessment engine. In the context of an increasingly expanding and constantly updated legal system, the need to accurately search, compare, and apply legal documents places significant pressure on state management agencies, officials, civil servants, and the business community. The application of AI in the legal field opens up new ways to leverage legal knowledge, supporting faster and more efficient work processing.

Within the framework of the program, CMC also signed cooperation agreements on science, technology, and innovation with the Hanoi Department of Science and Technology. The agreements aim to coordinate research and deployment of Clex and other Make in Vietnam AI solutions in state management, digital transformation, and legal support for businesses and citizens. This is a step towards expanding the application ecosystem and bringing Vietnamese technology products closer to the practical needs of each agency and organization. The articles do not state what further deployments or results will follow from the agreements. The articles do not state a date for the next phase of Clex's rollout.

stories.Headline: Anthropic report finds workers hide AI tricks from colleagues to protect jobs and time
stories.Summary:
Anthropic published a report on Monday saying that workers who develop highly effective AI tricks often have no incentive to share them with colleagues or bosses. Researchers interviewed 66 executives, managers and employees at 58 of Anthropic's corporate customers for the report. They found that many of those workers are reluctant to share their best AI tricks, citing reasons that range from job security to more leisure time. The practice has frustrated managers who are looking to exploit AI-driven efficiencies, the report says.

The report quotes one exasperated executive saying that workers do not want you to know because they want to use those 10 hours a week to go walk their dog. The report describes AI hoarding as a new form of the age-old workplace phenomenon of knowledge hiding, in which employees deliberately withhold information from their coworkers to retain a competitive edge. Employees in the AI age have even more at stake, their jobs, because if the trick they develop is powerful enough they might render themselves redundant. Even for those whose jobs are secure, revealing a time-saving trick might just mean they are assigned more work.

That raises a thorny question for business leaders about how to incentivize employees to help automate their own jobs. Employers hoping to discourage AI hoarding may need to rethink how they measure and reward productivity, according to the report. Otherwise, employees might realize that their most valuable professional asset is something they are better off keeping secret.

Articles.Title: Workers hoard AI knowledge to stay competitive, Anthropic report says

stories.headline_source: Workers hoard AI knowledge to stay competitive, Anthropic report says

stories.Headline: Sakana AI launches 30B Namazu Small model it says beats NVIDIA’s 120B Nemotron 3 Super on average
stories.Summary:
Sakana AI introduced Namazu Small, a 30-billion-parameter reasoning model, on November 25, 2026, according to Superpower Daily. Sakana says the model beat NVIDIA’s 120-billion-parameter Nemotron 3 Super on the overall average across 25 benchmarks. Sakana started with NVIDIA’s pretrained Nemotron 3 Nano and did continued pretraining and post-training in-house. The company compared Namazu Small with NVIDIA’s post-trained Nemotron 3 Nano and Nemotron 3 Super. Sakana describes Namazu Small as a reasoning model designed to organize information and work through complex questions step by step.

Namazu Small scored 73.5 on BrowseComp against Super’s 36.1, and 86.0 on LLM-jp LongBench against Super’s 60.0. It scored 78.3 on FaithEval, ahead of Super’s 59.1, but Super led LongBench v2 with 53.1 against Namazu Small’s 45.7. On SimpleQA Verified, Namazu Small scored 6.8 while Super scored 18.1, and on Japanese SimpleQA it scored 8.0 against Nano’s 9.2 and Super’s 24.9. Sakana says it expects to share on-premises availability details in early-to-mid December 2026, which is a date for more information, not a confirmed deployment date.

Sakana says recall from internal knowledge remains a weakness it plans to improve. It acknowledges that performance improved little on tasks answered from internal knowledge without outside information. Sakana says it will work on that capability while continuing to develop the model’s strengths. The company says it handled both continued pretraining and post-training in-house. Sakana says it combined techniques developed for its existing Namazu family with new training methods created for this model.

Sakana says the 30-billion-parameter size is intended to make the model practical for organizations running AI on their own infrastructure. Its stated goal is high performance with limited computing resources, enabling more organizations to use AI in their own environments. The development focus was everyday conversation, web-assisted research, long-document understanding and answers grounded in supplied evidence. Its intended work includes reading internal reports, gathering information across documents, answering questions and producing summaries with citations. It also includes investigating news or industry developments by searching repeatedly and organizing information from multiple sources into an answer.

The 25 benchmarks span web research, following instructions, understanding long documents, answering from evidence, and general or specialized knowledge. Sakana reports that Namazu Small beat both comparison models on the overall average, which is an average across different tasks, not a claim that the smaller model won every test. The model draws on research and development supported by Japan’s GENIAC project, run by METI and NEDO. Sakana plans to carry lessons from Namazu Small into future models and products. The company positions the model as a size companies can consider operating on their own computing infrastructure.

Sakana says it expects to share on-premises availability details in early-to-mid December 2026. The articles say the next concrete question is what those details say about access and timing. The articles leave open what those on-premises availability details will say about access and timing. The articles do not give a confirmed deployment date for the model. The articles do not state whether Namazu Small will be released for on-premises use.

stories.Headline: Nvidia delays RTX 60 series production to 2027 to prioritize AI hardware
stories.Summary:
Delays in the delivery of artificial intelligence graphics processing units have pushed the production of the RTX 60 series into 2027. This situation developed as reported on November 25, when information from Taiwan's Business Times indicated that demand for these products remains extremely tight. The shift in production schedules occurred because NVIDIA is prioritizing its high demand AI hardware over consumer gaming products. These supply chain constraints are now affecting the availability of several different hardware lines.

The current situation requires a reduction in the shipments of GeForce RTX 50 series gaming graphics processing units. Taiwanese original design manufacturers report that workstation superchip sets now face lead times of approximately 26 weeks. Specifically, the B300 model has an estimated lead time of 26 to 40 weeks, while the GB300 takes about 14 to 26 weeks. Orders placed during the last two quarters are not expected to arrive until the second or third quarter of next year.

Taiwanese original design manufacturers are responsible for reporting these lengthened delivery cycles for new orders. They stated that the extreme demand for AI products is significantly constraining the supply of consumer grade hardware. These manufacturers noted that the lead times for the B300 and GB300 have lengthened considerably. This reported shortage of components is what forces the delay of the RTX 60 series production.

This supply shift could alter the risk and reward profile for crypto miners who depend on these GPUs. Technical analysts suggest that people should monitor hardware price movements as a potential indicator of market sentiment. The overall impact depends on how the company manages the balance between AI and gaming chips. More to follow.

Articles.Title: NVIDIA AI GPU delivery delays push RTX 60 series production to 2027

stories.Headline: Jefferies says Meta's Muse shopping push could lift Instagram ad revenue
stories.Summary:
Jefferies published a research note on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, saying that Meta Platforms' artificial intelligence shopping push could lift advertising revenue on Instagram, and the broker kept a buy rating on the stock with an $875 price target. The note pointed to Meta's Muse assistant, which now handles Black Friday shopping at Walmart by finding deals, building a basket and completing the purchase once the shopper approves it. Jefferies cited Forter data showing that Muse placed 49% of the AI agent orders Forter tracked in the first full week of November. The broker's analysts also spotted a shopping option on a few Instagram Reels, where Muse found products linked by creators and offered viewers the option to buy.

Jefferies said the Reels feature might help Meta turn more ad views into purchases and encourage advertisers to spend more on Instagram. The broker considers the stock undervalued at 8.5 times forecast 2027 EBITDA on an enterprise value basis, compared with an average of 13.3 times for peers. Jefferies also sees room for Meta to exceed the consensus forecast of 17% sequential revenue growth in the fourth quarter of 2026, which sits below its pre-pandemic seasonal range of 19% to 26%. The assistant is now available in Singapore, Australia and the UK, with plans to bring Muse to the company's glasses in Australia and the UK.

Jefferies analysts are the ones making the revenue case, and the note carries their buy rating and their $875 price target on Meta shares. The broker's analysts described the Instagram Reels shopping option as a feature that might convert more ad views into purchases and draw more advertiser spending to the platform. Jefferies based part of its view on Forter data about the share of AI agent orders Muse placed in early November. The note also set out the broker's valuation comparison and its forecast for fourth quarter revenue growth.

The note follows other coverage of Muse, including a Jefferies report a month earlier saying the assistant was blocked by one-third of websites tested and a Wedbush view that e-commerce adoption remains uncertain. Meta has said Muse raises conversions for advertisers, according to one report, and chief executive Mark Zuckerberg has said the assistant will take a small fee from transactions. Amazon and Meta are negotiating the future of AI shopping, according to another report, while consumers are not quite there yet. The articles do not say what Meta or Jefferies plans to do next beyond the UK and Australia glasses rollout.

Articles.Title: Meta’s AI shopping push could lift Instagram ad revenue, Jefferies says

stories.Headline: Orange CTO Bruno Zerbib warns against Nokia and Nvidia AI-RAN GPU tie-up
stories.Summary:
Nokia and Nvidia formed a tie-up to develop AI-RAN products using graphics processing units. This partnership became a point of concern for Orange CTO Bruno Zerbib in November 2026. Zerbib raised these warnings during the annual OpenTech event held in Paris. The event featured senior executives from Nokia, Ericsson, and Orange. The discussion focused on the risks of this specific technical architecture.

Nokia is designing 5G and 6G products based on Nvidia GPUs for Layer 1 functions. This follows a one billion dollar investment by Nvidia into Nokia last year. Nvidia also invested ten billion dollars into xAI in January and two billion into Marvell. Furthermore, Nvidia provided five billion dollars to Intel for central processing unit development. These changes replace custom silicon with commercially unproven GPUs in the radio access network.

Bruno Zerbib runs the technology division and strategy for the French operator Orange. He stated he must avoid a risky architecture change that offers zero benefits. Zerbib expressed concern over a subscription model for software updates on top of capex. He also questioned if an American company would impact the sovereignty of a European vendor. The CTO claimed he does not believe in magic regarding promised efficiency gains.

Alok Tripathi, an independent analyst, said the era of high-profile GPU AI-RAN marketing may end. This view follows reports that Nvidia dumped 56 percent of its stake in Nokia. This divestment triggered a four percent drop in the share price of the Finnish vendor. Telcos are affected because they may rely on Nvidia for ongoing software optimizations. Some experts are unconvinced that the highest promised efficiency figures are actually achievable.

Nokia and Ericsson have been substituting adaptive AI software for algorithms written by humans. Nokia promised spectral efficiency improvements of 20 percent this year and 50 percent next year. The company claims a doubling of this efficiency will occur by the year 2028. Nokia's CTO Pallavi Mahajan says GPUs allow operators to rely on software upgrades for years. However, Nokia indicated it will not develop custom silicon to succeed its latest product.

Nokia advisor Harri Holma says there is no hurry for operators to replace current chips. The articles leave open whether telcos can directly monetize the use of these GPUs. It remains unclear what happens to workers who refined the old human-written algorithms. Zerbib is not yet picking sides regarding the deployment of Nokia for AI-RAN. The impact of Nvidia's potential loss of investment ability on the economy is unknown.

Articles.Title: Nokia tie-up with Nvidia on AI-RAN gets warning from Orange CTO

stories.Headline: Anthropic shares close below $83 IPO price as analysts initiate bullish coverage
stories.Summary:
Anthropic shares closed down 6.5% on Tuesday, falling below the artificial intelligence company's $83 IPO price, after the stock had opened at $111.50 on the Nasdaq on Thursday. The AI lab raised $81.3 billion in what the article calls the largest offering of all time, and investors had eagerly awaited the debut in hopes it would revitalize the broader AI trade. The offering was oversubscribed, and roughly half of the institutional investors that placed orders were left empty-handed, yet those firms do not appear to be racing to scoop up shares as the market wavers. Chip stocks Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices and Intel, as well as neoclouds CoreWeave, IREN and Nebius, all fell during intraday trading on Tuesday.

Canaccord Genuity initiated coverage of Anthropic with a buy rating and a $135 price target, saying the analysts believe the company is building one of the most important enterprise technology franchises of the AI era. They wrote that the opportunity is considerably larger than traditional software spending, while noting that the risks are unusually large, particularly around infrastructure commitments and the durability of competitive differentiation. Wedbush analysts initiated coverage with an outperform rating and a $120 price target on Monday, saying Anthropic went public in a tumultuous market as debate around the AI buildout continues. Oppenheimer initiated coverage with an outperform rating and a $150 price target on Tuesday, citing growing enterprise AI spending, improving compute efficiency and a multi-chip strategy.

The analysts said they expect Anthropic to navigate the competitive environment and capture a uniquely large addressable market, with Wedbush writing that the genie is out of the bottle and that ANT is a strong play on that theme. Oppenheimer said its bullish stance stems from its belief that Anthropic will capture growing enterprise AI spending and that rising customer adoption creates a substantial runway for the company. The Oppenheimer analysts added that while competition and compute commitments remain risks, they believe Anthropic can translate its leadership into durable growth and operating leverage. The article gives no further context on what happens next beyond the analysts' coverage and price targets.

Articles.Title: Anthropic closes below $83 IPO price, but analysts are still largely positive

stories.Headline: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO as it pushes beyond GPUs into agent security
stories.Summary:
Nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO on Nov. 23, after an 11-day absence, TechTarget reported on Nov. 25, 2026. Huang is back as Nvidia CEO as the company moves beyond GPUs into agent security and AI infrastructure. The article said enterprises must decide how much of their AI stack to hand over to the chip giant. Nvidia began shipping its next-generation Vera Rubin computing platform in November. In October, Nvidia expanded its collaboration with Oracle to bring the platform to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure at a multi-gigawatt scale.

Nvidia’s revenue for the third quarter of fiscal 2027 reached $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier, including $107.6 billion from data centers. In its Nov. 17 earnings report, Nvidia said its Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, which extend its architecture to CPUs and networking, had begun shipping. On Oct. 27, Nvidia and Oracle outlined plans to expand Oracle Cloud Infrastructure’s Vera Rubin deployments to multi-gigawatt scale. The plans support model training, inference and the CPU-intensive tasks agents perform between model calls. On Oct. 21, Nvidia introduced an OpenShell reference architecture combining Vera Rubin infrastructure, BlueField-4 DPUs, OpenShell runtime software and the Nvidia Sentry security framework.

On Nov. 10, Nvidia contributed OpenShell, its open source runtime for securing and governing AI agents, to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation. OpenShell restricts agents’ access to data, credentials and networks, while Nvidia Sentry detects when agents move outside those boundaries. David Wang, COO and head of product and go-to-market at Tetrate, said people tend to understate how important it has always been to Jensen to build ecosystems around his hardware and software. Wang said Nvidia’s relatively open approach to software development makes it difficult for Nvidia to control the broader ecosystem. Wang said it might be hard for Nvidia to have a stranglehold on the software ecosystem around its GPUs.

Emily Hartstone, founder of the Hartstone Institute and Runtime Authority Control, said contributing OpenShell to the CNCF puts agent sandboxing on a path toward becoming shared infrastructure. Hartstone said standardizing how agents are contained does not resolve questions about who has the authority to approve their actions. She illustrated the distinction with a customer service agent that can issue refunds, where a $40 refund for a damaged order could fall within its authority. A $4,800 refund to a recently opened account might require additional approval, even though the agent can technically process both. Hartstone said someone has to have approved refunds of that size, for that customer, under those conditions, and that approval has to still stand today.

The article said Huang has long pursued a strategy of making Nvidia’s technology central to how enterprises build and operate AI systems. It said CIOs must weigh the benefits of an integrated platform against vendor dependence and control over their technology stacks. Wang pointed to gaming, where Nvidia gave developers tools to build more sophisticated games that required more powerful GPUs. Wang said Nvidia is applying a similar strategy to enterprise AI by extending its software stack into model serving, security, traffic routing and infrastructure efficiency. Tetrate, Wang’s company, provides software that helps route traffic on Nvidia’s BlueField DPUs, and Tetrate is an Nvidia customer and partner.

Hartstone said organizations must define permissions, limits and exceptions in advance, with systems enforcing those rules when agents act. She said companies also need records showing what an agent did, which authority it relied on and what rules applied. The article said buyers must evaluate agent infrastructure on more than containment, including how it handles identity, action-level authorization and accountability across the applications and environments agents use. Hartstone said any vendor can show you an agent doing something, and said to ask to see it refuse an action it has the access to take but no authority for, and ask who decided. The article said whether Nvidia can turn its hardware, software and infrastructure investments into a more comprehensive enterprise AI platform will help determine how much of the technology stack it ultimately controls.

Articles.Title: Nvidia’s AI strategy now hinges on Huang more than ever

stories.Headline: Nvidia governance concerns and potential import tariffs drive AI investor anxiety and market declines
stories.Summary:
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq indices ended lower on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, as investor anxiety regarding artificial intelligence resurfaced. The S&P 500 fell about 0.5 percent to 7,201.09, while the Nasdaq 100 dropped 2 percent to 26,214.17. This downturn followed a previous session of optimism regarding the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as the chief executive officer of Nvidia. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.9 percent to 49,595.31, and the Russell 2000 ended 0.6 percent higher.

The market decline was driven by concerns over governance issues at Nvidia and the possibility of new import tariffs from President Trump. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer may release results as soon as Tuesday from a months-long subsidy inquiry. This investigation covers industrial subsidies in China, the 27-nation European Union, and 14 other countries. The Trump administration is reportedly moving toward higher import duties on trading partners that Washington claims disadvantage American manufacturers. Semiconductor ETFs fell between 7.3 percent and 16 percent, with Nvidia leading those losses.

U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche pushed back against claims that Nvidia or Jensen Huang are under criminal investigation. He refused to provide further details regarding the chipmaker during his statements on Tuesday. Diana Baechle of SimCorp told CNBC that market volatility will likely continue because there are many unknowns. Meanwhile, Dell Technologies reported record third-quarter revenue and raised its full-year FY27 revenue target for the third time this year.

The broader market remains volatile as investors weigh these governance and trade concerns against other corporate developments. RBC Capital Markets analyst Ken Herbert expects a deal between Tesla and SpaceX by early 2027. Seaport Global Securities also issued a bullish endorsement for Tesla, claiming robotaxi operations could become a multibillion-dollar business by the end of next year. Additionally, TG Therapeutics reached an all-time high after the FDA accepted an application for its drug Briumvi.

stories.Headline: Anthropic finds bosses pushing AI at work fuels surveillance fears and worker resistance
stories.Summary:
Anthropic, the AI startup, published a 29-page report on 24 November 2026 finding that when bosses push AI at work, it can fuel workers' surveillance fears and cause resistance, according to Business Insider. Researchers conducted 66 interviews with 58 companies that are Anthropic customers, and the report said pushback can lead to what it called abandoned or fragile automations. At one law firm, the chief operating officer asked a staffer to build an AI tool to check for conflicts of interest, which left workers handling tricky cases they had previously handed to attorneys, and the firm dropped the tool and resumed its prior process after workers pushed back. One operations supervisor told researchers he began each day with an AI-generated report on how much work each member of his 12-person team completed and how often they made errors, saying he could then question them about any lag. Some interviewees thought AI could make performance feedback more accurate but also worried about how closely it could let bosses track employees.

People at two-thirds of the companies told Anthropic they were hiring less because of AI, with a third of those decreases coming from companies leaving roles unfilled after workers left and most stemming from companies skipping hires they would have made without AI. Interviewees at five companies discussed pushing out workers who would not adopt AI, and at two companies interviewees said AI automation eliminated a position, resulting in someone losing a job. One engineering leader said a couple of people started off extremely anti-AI and moved along the spectrum but not enough, so the company let them go. Ten companies said they had stepped up hiring because of AI, mainly to help roll it out or to boost IT support.

One operations manager said she woke at 3 a.m. worried about her career prospects and asked Claude how to set herself apart so that AI could not do everything she does. The report said letting workers experiment on their own brought its own problems, since a tool that saved one person time did not necessarily help others and apps workers built still needed someone to review and maintain them. At one law firm, a paralegal recalled partners asking how he prompted AI after noticing his demand letters stood out, and although he eventually shared his approach, his first instinct was to keep it to himself.

Articles.Title: Bosses pushing AI can fuel workers' surveillance fears, Anthropic report finds

stories.Headline: Microsoft posts $45.9 billion operating income as Nadella calls Copilot the new OS for work
stories.Summary:
TipRanks published an article on November 24, 2026, saying Microsoft seems to be one of the safest ways to invest in artificial intelligence. The article said Microsoft posted $45.9 billion in operating income in Q1 2027. It said CEO Satya Nadella recently remarked that the company thinks of Copilot as the new operating system for work. The author said the recent tech sell-off made Microsoft's valuation especially appealing. The author rated MSFT stock a Buy.

The article said Microsoft's revenue grew 19% year-over-year to $92.3 billion in its Fiscal Q1 2027 results. It said operating income increased 21% to $45.9 billion and adjusted earnings per share rose 18% to $4.89. It said Microsoft Cloud revenue climbed 30% to $63.9 billion and Azure accelerated to 48% growth, with guidance for 49% to 50% constant-currency growth this quarter. It said daily Copilot users increased nearly 50% sequentially and more than fivefold year-over-year, and customers with over 50,000 Copilot seats increased more than eightfold year-over-year. It said Foundry passed 120,000 customers, with revenue more than tripling year-over-year, and customers building agentic applications with multiple models increased fivefold year-over-year.

The article said Nadella remarked that the company thinks of Copilot as the new OS for work. The author said he liked that ambition but also liked the existing business behind it. The author said Microsoft has built multiple ways to win as enterprises adopt AI. The author said Microsoft relies on cash-flowing legacy subscriptions to fund a full-stack AI ecosystem. The author said he remains Bullish.

The article said Volkswagen's planned rollout to over 330,000 employees is one example of broader deployment. It said Microsoft has $677 billion in remaining commercial performance obligations. It said operating cash flow reached $58 billion, leaving $18.6 billion of free cash flow after cash investment. It said Wall Street rates MSFT a Strong Buy, based on 35 Buys and four Holds, and the $632.48 average price target implies roughly 28% upside from today's price levels. It said Microsoft's quarterly capex reached $45.2 billion, including finance leases.

The article said Microsoft pushed Copilot further into practical work at its Ignite conference in November. It said the company rolled out a unified starting hub in Copilot that merges Chat for quick queries with Cowork for longer, multi-step projects. It said Microsoft was preparing a broad rollout of Copilot Code in the coming weeks so everyday employees can build custom apps without writing code. It said updates to Agent 365 help IT teams manage permissions and track return on investment across Microsoft and third-party agents, while Microsoft IQ links those agents to a company's internal knowledge and workflows. It said Copilot's Auto mode automatically routes user prompts to whichever model offers the best balance of speed, capability, and cost for a given task.

The article said MSFT trades at 24.59x Fiscal 2027 consensus EPS of $20.03, falling to 20.33x Fiscal 2028 EPS of $24.23 and 16.31x Fiscal 2029 EPS of $30.20. It said consensus expects roughly 16% EPS growth this year, followed by nearly 21% and 25%. It said adjusted EPS of $4.89 beat the latest $4.72 forecast, and the preceding quarter delivered $4.74 against $4.24 expected. It said competition from Amazon and Google remains intense and other enterprise AI platforms are also competing for customers. It said infrastructure costs could pressure cloud margins and Copilot adoption might slow.

stories.Headline: Trump suggests US government take equity stake in Nvidia to ensure AI leadership
stories.Summary:
President Donald Trump suggested the US government could take an equity stake in Nvidia. He made these comments during an interview with the New York Post. The remarks were published on November 24, 2026. Trump stated he has considered this idea but has not yet proposed it. He believes it might not be too late to raise the issue.

The plan would involve federal ownership of the chipmaker to ensure American AI leadership. Trump also mentioned he would pardon CEO Jensen Huang if it became necessary. He expects Huang to be fine without a pardon during his testimony. This testimony before Congress is scheduled to take place next week. Trump previously pressed the Nvidia board to reinstate Huang.

President Trump said the success of Nvidia is central to keeping the United States ahead. He told Huang to tell the truth to lawmakers during his upcoming testimony. Trump added that Huang would not need to invoke his Fifth Amendment rights. He noted that the Nvidia stock recovered much of its Tuesday loss. These comments were made while reviewing market data from the Oval Office.

Investors may see White House backing as a floor for the strategic position of Nvidia. Others could view the move as a source of political entanglement and governance risk. This risk involves China sales and export rules for the semiconductor company. Global chip peers and other governments are also watching these potential steps. The wider semiconductor and Nasdaq complex face elevated headline risk.

Washington previously took an equity stake in Intel in 2025 to secure domestic capacity. This was part of a push for critical supply chains and semiconductor production. Nvidia is a dominant supplier of chips that power AI data centres. It is also one of the most valuable companies in the world. The government has shown willingness to take stakes in strategically important firms.

The structure, size, and purpose of any potential government stake remain entirely open. It is unknown how Nvidia shareholders and the board would respond to this. Huang's testimony next week will be a marker for the AI trade. Further follow-up from the White House is expected regarding this potential policy. The articles leave the final decision on the equity stake undecided.

stories.Summary:
President Donald Trump intervened to reinstate Jensen Huang as the CEO of Nvidia. This action followed a meeting between Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping. The event occurred around September 24, 2026, in Washington, DC. Trump hosted a state dinner for Xi and Peng Liyuan. The dinner took place in the East Room of the White House.

The situation involves claims that Alice Huang may have worked for Chinese intelligence. Trump bought shares of Nvidia and weakened AI chip controls on China. Huang previously traveled to see Xi and argued for selling chips to China. The Biden administration had initiated the chip controls to slow Chinese AI. These controls targeted chips as the best lever for slowing Chinese development.

The US government reportedly informed Trump that Huang may be compromised by China. Sources told reporters that Huang had an affair with a woman linked to intelligence. Trump showed evident sympathy for a powerful man facing consequences for bad behavior. The Nvidia board fused profits, corruption, and sex into a unified hyper-spectacle. This combination includes policy capture and the influence of the Chinese Communist Party.

US voters moved away from Republicans due to corruption and AI issues. Policy thinkers expressed concern that China could get ahead of the US. Some advocates believe smuggled semiconductors are a dire national security threat to America. Others suggest these are violations of export controls with government officials looking away. Members of Congress are now entering the vortex of this complex scandal.

The Biden administration first started the chip controls to limit Chinese AI growth. The US government pinpointed specific chips to hinder the development of Chinese models. Some believe that Nvidia GPUs are crucial for achieving godlike artificial intelligence power. Others suggest that the current trajectory of AI development may eventually plateau. There are assumptions that Chinese access to chips endangers the United States.

Congressional investigators will now examine the details of the spy-sex scandal. They may also investigate the existential risks associated with artificial intelligence development. The legal process may help separate real events from the integrated hyper-spectacle. It remains uncertain if Alice Huang worked directly for the Ministry of State Security. stories.Headline: Mayor Zohran Mamdani warns that the stock market is overly dependent on AI stocks
stories.Summary:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani commented on Monday about the corporate turbulence involving the chipmaker Nvidia and its chief executive officer, Jensen Huang. The company experienced a dramatic drop in share price when Huang stepped down as the chief executive officer on 12 November. This resignation followed reports that Huang had an extramarital relationship with Alice Huang, a tech executive suspected of being a Chinese spy. After Donald Trump intervened, the California based company reinstated Huang on Monday and saw its value bounce back by 31.5 percent.

The situation involves Alice Huang, who is accused of routing advanced chips to Beijing through her company called Megaspeed. National intelligence director Jay Clayton stated that he suspected China was able to obtain the most advanced artificial intelligence chips from Nvidia. Mayor Mamdani noted that a rumored divorce settlement of 81 billion dollars could provide universal childcare for every three and four year old in the United States for one year. He also mentioned that Jensen Huang and his wife, Lori Huang, have been married since 1985 and hold combined assets of about 160 billion dollars.

Mayor Mamdani stated that the stock market is disproportionately dependent on stocks related to the artificial intelligence boom powered by Nvidia chips. He expressed concern about the dominance of this technology and said working Americans did not sign up for pensions tied to the fidelity of Jensen Huang. The mayor referenced Justice Louis Brandeis to argue that democracy and great wealth concentrated in the hands of a few cannot both exist. He believes the recent volatility shows a massive impact on the lives of working people across the entire country.

President Donald Trump told the Wall Street Journal that he likes getting involved in companies to help them when they have problems. He pointed to the government taking a 10 percent stake in the chipmaker Intel as an example of his approach. Congress is now expected to grill Jensen Huang regarding his ties with China and the intervention by the president. The situation highlights a complex relationship between the democratic socialist mayor and the financial center of Wall Street.
