stories.Headline: Amazon Cognito lets services and AI agents exchange tokens to act for users
stories.Summary:
Amazon Web Services announced on November 24, 2026, a new OAuth token exchange feature in Amazon Cognito that lets services and AI agents call APIs on behalf of users, with Cognito acting as the OAuth 2.0 authorization server. The feature is built on OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange as defined in RFC 8693, and it addresses the second hop that happens when a service handling a user's request needs to call a further downstream service. In the post's example, a restaurant review app books a table and its reservation service must email details to friends, and the question is which token the reservation service should use when it calls the email API. Forwarding the user's access token hides the reservation service, while the service's own client credentials token loses the user's identity, and token exchange resolves that by returning a new issued token that identifies the user and can also name the calling service.

Every exchange starts with a subject token representing the user, which in Cognito can be an access token or ID token issued by the user pool to the app where the user signed in, and the calling service sends it to Cognito to receive a new token for the downstream resource server. The feature supports two patterns, impersonation and delegation, and the calling service chooses based on whether the downstream API needs to authorize the service acting for the user. In impersonation the calling service does not identify itself as the actor, so the issued token represents the user and carries a client_id claim but no act claim, which fits a backend for frontend that only relays requests. In delegation the calling service also sends an actor token, and Cognito adds an act claim naming the calling service so the resource server can see and log who authorized the action and who carried it out, which the post describes as the important pattern for AI agents.

The exchange can be requested at the /oauth2/token endpoint on the user pool's domain or through the GetDerivedToken API with an AWS SDK, which does not require a user pool domain, and both accept the same subject token, actor token, audience and scopes and return an issued token with the same claims. Cognito validates every exchange before issuing a token, checking the subject token's signature and expiry and refusing a token that has been revoked or that belongs to a disabled user in the user pool. The post advises resource servers to accept a delegated token only when the act.client_id reflects a service they trust and matches the token's client_id, meaning the trusted service requested the token itself. The post also describes how the feature works with a Model Context Protocol server and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity, and it explains that with token exchange each hop gets only the scopes it needs while the email API can see which service acted for the user.

Articles.Title: Delegate user access to AI agents with Amazon Cognito token exchange

stories.headline_source: Delegate user access to AI agents with Amazon Cognito token exchange

stories.Headline: Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia and sparks a 30 percent share rally
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia, and the move set off a large relief rally that pushed Nvidia shares up more than 30 percent and lifted the Nasdaq Composite index by 6.5 percent on Monday, according to CNBC, which published the report on Tuesday, November 24, 2026. Both the stock and the wider market pulled back the following day, the article said. The bounce came after a week of panic selling in tech that spilled over into almost every other sector and revived fears of a rapid unwind in the AI trade, the report said. Short-covering and oversold technical conditions helped fuel Monday's recovery, and the article said the market may lose steam once those forces peter out.

Glen Smith, chief investment officer at GDS Wealth Management, said the decision to reinstate Huang helps remove a key level of uncertainty from the AI trade, according to the article. Mary Ann Bartels, chief investment strategist at Sanctuary Wealth, said the rebound does not mean the correction is over. The article said the selloff also raised doubts about how much profit AI can deliver amid rising costs and slowing data center construction. Brian Stutland, portfolio manager at Equity Armor Investments, said Huang's return resolves the leadership question, but export rules, financing costs and returns on AI spending still have to be worked out, and he said he still wants to own stocks and some protection.

The article described several ways investors could hedge, including healthcare stocks, which it said are up an average 15 percent this year, and utilities, which it said have gained around 8 percent since the end of September while the Nasdaq 100 shed 17 percent before Monday's rally. It said the iShares Core U.S. Aggregate Bond ETF has gained 2.3 percent on a total return basis since the end of September, and it cited Truist strategist Keith Lerner favoring long-duration U.S. Treasuries. It said the iShares MSCI India ETF has gained more than 11 percent over the past month, and it cited J.P. Morgan's Rajiv Batra describing India in a September report as emerging as an AI hedge. The article did not say what happens next beyond the factors it listed.

Articles.Title: Nvidia revived the AI trade, but investors still have reasons to hedge

stories.Headline: Cyber insurers say AI phishing kits drive rising claims as premiums stay flat
stories.Summary:
Cyber insurance providers are approaching 2027 facing a fundamental challenge, according to Dark Reading. Claims rose 40% in 2024 and another 20% in 2025, even as premiums have stayed largely flat. Coalition and Travelers both say this trend isn't sustainable. At the center of that shift is AI, which is reshaping the threat landscape. AI is making ransomware, business email compromise and phishing dramatically easier to execute at scale.

Dark Reading media and projects director Becky Bracken and senior news director Rob Wright hosted the Dark Reading Confidential episode. They sat down with Lauren Winchester, vice president of cyber-risk services at Travelers, and Daniel Woods, head of emerging risk at Coalition. Woods said the National Association of Insurance Commissioners publishes an annual report about the US market. That report shows the number of policies being issued is growing while the amount of premium being collected is pretty much stable. Woods said claims rose 40% in 2024 and 20% in 2025.

Woods said the cyber-insurance market is beginning to ask whether prices are sustainable, especially given changes related to AI. Winchester said the industry is at a period of uncertainty right now, as most industries are. She said AI is likely to change a lot of the ways people work and the ways threat actors engage with and attack companies. She said that uncertainty is something the industry is grappling with. Woods said AI is a general-purpose technology that impacts not just the exploitation of vulnerabilities but other mechanisms.

Winchester said it is important not to conflate the surge in vulnerabilities being disclosed with a surge in attacks that drive cyber claims, at least not just yet. She said CISA had added 246 known exploited vulnerabilities in 2026 through Sept. 30, which exceeded the 245 added in total for 2025. She said the figure may be about a third more than last year by the end of the year. She said ransomware leak site activity for Q3 2026 was up, with 111 distinct groups posting victims. She said there was a record number of 2,882 victims on leak sites, 26% up from the prior quarter and the highest quarter ever seen.

Woods attributed an increase in business email compromise to EvilTokens, a new AI phishing kit released in February of this year. He said it was sold as a SaaS business model and did not exploit vulnerabilities. He said it used AI to create convincing phishing lures by email or replica websites, manipulating users into letting attackers in even with MFA enforced. He said a blockchain tracking company found the operators earned $1.1 million in revenue from other criminals buying their services.

Winchester said the industry sees that in the ransomware ecosystem, where there is ransomware-as-a-service. The articles say the conversation moves past the headline-grabbing surge in disclosed vulnerabilities to a more nuanced picture. They say exploitation is rising, but not as sharply as disclosure volume. They say AI-powered phishing kits are being sold SaaS-style to criminals with little technical skill, driving a measurable spike in BEC and ransomware activity.

The two insurers agree the real exposure lies not necessarily with large enterprises, which have the resources to track threat intelligence and patch quickly. They say it lies with small and mid-sized businesses that often lack an in-house IT team altogether. The articles say insurers now have to step in, not just to underwrite risk but to actively help policyholders defend their organizations. They say that awareness gap is where insurers have to step in.

The transcript was edited for clarity and length by Informa TechTarget's internal AI assistant. The articles direct readers to listen to the podcast or watch the video for the full experience. The articles say Winchester and Woods were asked to unpack what the data actually shows. The articles leave open when the tools will become even further identified and to what extent, and who will be doing that.

Articles.Title: Cyber Insurers See a New AI Divide - Dark Reading

stories.Headline: VBA official Derek Herbert outlines plans to speed disability claims with earlier records and AI
stories.Summary:
The Veterans Benefits Administration is modernizing its data infrastructure and exploring artificial intelligence in an effort to speed up disability claims processing, the agency announced. Derek Herbert, the VBA's chief production officer, outlined the plans and described how the agency intends to change the way it handles records. The agency wants to obtain military personnel and medical records as soon as service members transition to veteran status. The goal is to put the new process in place within the next year, according to Herbert.

The change is meant to eliminate the delays that come from requesting records only after a claim has been filed, and it is also expected to reduce the administrative burden on claims processors. Herbert said accurate, well-organized data and scalable infrastructure are essential if the agency is to adopt AI successfully. AI could help summarize records, identify relevant information and automate administrative tasks, he said. Herbert cautioned that the technology will not replace human claims adjudicators.

Herbert, who leads production work at the VBA, is the official responsible for describing the plans and their goals. He framed the effort around getting records earlier and building a data foundation that AI tools can rely on. He also made clear that people will remain part of the process, saying AI will not take the place of human claims adjudicators. The articles do not say what the effort will cost or which contractors, if any, are involved.

The articles give no further context on the timing beyond the one-year goal Herbert described, and they do not say what happens next beyond that target. The VBA's plans rest on obtaining records at the point of transition and on infrastructure that can handle the data at scale. Whether the agency meets its one-year goal is not stated in the articles. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics gives students and staff 100 million weekly AI tokens
stories.Summary:
The Shanghai University of Finance and Economics announced on November 21 that it is providing free AI tokens to all campus members. This new initiative gives every student and staff member a weekly allowance of up to 100 million tokens. The university intends for these digital resources to become a standard part of teaching, similar to books or lab equipment. Users can access various AI models and tools by signing into the university website with their campus IDs. The program allows students to use these tokens for cleaning data, debugging code, conducting research, and building AI agents.

This move follows a broader trend among Chinese universities that began earlier this fall to provide computing power as a public resource. For example, Tsinghua University started offering 1,000 yuan in computing vouchers to its members this September. Peking University provides 3,000 monthly credits and a year of free access to the Qoder AI coding assistant. Additionally, Hunan University gives students 2 million tokens daily, and Tongji University launched a 100 million weekly token plan in October. University officials and experts believe that computing platforms and data centers will become essential infrastructure for future schools.

Xue Lan, the dean of the Institute for AI International Governance at Tsinghua University, noted that these tools may eventually be as important as libraries or gyms. However, Zhang Duanhong from the Center for Educational Policy Research at Tongji University argued that the true value lies in the learning advanced rather than the number of tokens used. Some researchers worry that free access could lead to idle teaching where AI generates both the assignments and the answers. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Trustly raises $60 million to use AI for real-time financial intelligence
stories.Summary:
Trustly, a provider of Pay by Bank payments, said on Tuesday, Nov. 24, that it has raised $60 million in new capital, according to a news release from the company. The company said the financing will support its work to bring together payment and data services and to use artificial intelligence to embed real-time financial intelligence. Trustly said the funding will boost the development of new products that use AI to turn payments into intelligence, helping businesses win new customers, retain them for longer and stay ahead of risk. The company also said it supports more than $120 billion in transactions a year and that it announced earlier this year it had surpassed 120 million customers worldwide. The release ties the raise to Trustly's stated goal of combining payments and data services, with the CEO saying the money supports that work and the use of AI to embed real-time financial intelligence.

The company said the new products would use AI to turn payments into intelligence, which it said would help businesses win new customers, retain them for longer and stay ahead of risk. Trustly said it supports more than $120 billion in transactions a year, and it said it had surpassed 120 million customers worldwide earlier this year. The articles give no further terms of the raise, such as investors or valuation. Trustly CEO Johan Tjärnberg said in the release that the financing will support the company's work to bring together payment and data services and use AI to embed real-time financial intelligence. The release added that the funding will boost development of new products that leverage AI to turn payments into intelligence, helping businesses win new customers, retain them for longer and stay ahead of risk.

The company described the raise as new capital and did not name the investors involved. The articles place the raise alongside earlier research that PYMNTS Intelligence did with Trustly this year, in the report "Pay by Bank Deep Dive: Digital Bank Users Are Ready to Switch." That report found that 35.4% of digital bank users' account-to-account transactions could move to Pay by Bank if offered discounts and buyer protection, compared with 25.3% for the full sample. For bill payments, the estimates came to 32% for digital bank users and 22% overall, and roughly 43% of digital bank users named immediate cash benefits as their chief reason for using Pay by Bank, while 16.9% pointed to buyer protection. The report also found that just 12.2% of all bank customers said they saw Pay by Bank as a substitute for debit, but with rewards, buyer protection or both, 72% either already see it that way or would under at least one of those conditions.

stories.Summary:
HR Executive published an article on November 24, 2026, about what it calls shadow AI, which it describes as employees using artificial intelligence tools at work without the knowledge or approval of their employer. The article presents this practice as a growing problem for HR departments, though it gives no figures on how many workers do it or how often. stories.Headline: Beijing universities provide students with free AI tools and computing resources
stories.Summary:
Several universities in Beijing have started providing students with free access to artificial intelligence tools and computing resources since the beginning of the fall semester. Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications gave freshmen free access to over a dozen large AI models and tools for developing AI agents through a campus platform. Students are utilizing these resources to debug code, review academic literature, and troubleshoot various experiments. One senior student, Zhang Jing, created an automated tool that summarizes research methods from newly published academic papers each week.

Peking University announced in October that faculty and students would receive free access to AI-powered coding agents for one year with a monthly usage allowance. Tsinghua University launched a computing power voucher program that provides eligible students and faculty an initial allowance of 1,000 yuan, or 152 dollars. These vouchers allow users to rent graphics processing unit resources, use computing clusters, and access AI models through application programming interfaces. The university plans to make 30 million yuan, or 4.57 million dollars, worth of computing resources available over the next three years.

Xue Lan, the dean of Schwarzman College at Tsinghua University, stated that computing platforms and data centers could become key infrastructure for universities in the future. Tian Xuan, the dean of Peking University's Guanghua School of Management, argued that students must focus more on asking meaningful questions and exercising critical judgment. To protect academic integrity, Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications now requires students to disclose how they use AI in their reports and papers. Tsinghua University has also restricted the use of its computing power vouchers to noncommercial activities like coursework and academic research.

Articles.Title: Beijing universities offer students free AI computing resources - China Daily Global Edition

stories.Headline: Anthropic accuses a company of model distillation
stories.Summary:
A user posting as weli said on Hacker News on 24 November 2026 that Anthropic is accusing them and their company of using Anthropic's API for distillation, and that they are not doing so. The poster said their company does not train its own models. The poster said their only usage that could get them flagged is automated regression benchmarks run whenever they change some AI settings. The poster said this is not against Anthropic's policy. The poster said they now have 24 hours to prove they did not distill.

The post was submitted 3 hours before it was read and had 150 points and 93 comments. The poster asked how to prove they are not distilling Anthropic models without breaking their users' privacy. One commenter suggested submitting the same evidence to Claude and asking it whether it is sufficient to make distilling seem unlikely. Another commenter suggested vetting the evidence with a second, adversarial Claude session. A commenter said they skip straight to a second Claude session to review their code.

A commenter warned that Anthropic will read their logs and determine the evidence is an attempt to distill. Commenters said Anthropic will use a Claude agent to review the submission anyway. One commenter suggested migrating to Bedrock via AWS, saying a serious bill brings a dedicated account rep who is an actual human being. A commenter said Bedrock is not zero data retention, linking a Claude support article. A commenter said zero data retention does not necessarily help, because a single prompt can still flag an account.

A commenter said AWS still runs automated checks on input and output even when Bedrock is zero data retention. A commenter said they would not be surprised if Anthropic builds a cumulative risk score that predicts distillation without retaining data. A commenter said a carve-out permits retention of data that fails a risk score for breaking laws or attempting to violate safety. A commenter said dropping whole accounts for bad prompts would become a new attack vector. A commenter asked what the point is of continuing to give money to a company that treats you this way.

A commenter said switching providers cannot be done overnight. A commenter said switching is not as easy as changing an API key, because you must find everything you tested with one model and make sure it still works. A commenter said they set up evals early and are saving 50% or more by routing tasks properly. A commenter said that if quality matters you must re-tweak settings and prompts for whichever model you switch to. A commenter said models do not all work the same or in the same order for all tasks.

A commenter asked whether the poster had lost their API keys, suggesting someone stole them and is running distillation. A commenter said a stolen key would have produced a surprise bill. A commenter said a distillation attack might be hidden in a lot of usage, spread across many keys to avoid discovery. A commenter doubted that most big corporations, let alone startups, audit bills against internal metrics. A commenter said they were doing innocuous work on IRS forms and had a subagent flagged for "reasoning extraction".

A commenter said asking the model to look at past session transcripts, export earlier chats as HTML pages or look at tool calls from previous sessions seems to trigger an overeager classifier. A commenter said competition is needed because being locked out by a single leading AI provider is a death sentence. A commenter disagreed, saying you can get Claude through Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry, or use GPT, Grok, Gemini, GLM, Kimi, Mistral or open weight models. A commenter said proving a negative is hard and suggested telling Anthropic what you have been doing and asking what part is an issue. A commenter said Big Tech refuses to do this, calling the risk department judge, jury and executioner.

A commenter said they started building their company after a similar message, realizing they could not depend on one provider. A commenter said distillation attacks are spread throughout numerous accounts and the poster has likely triggered some detection. A commenter said the best approach is to show the work is part of a real project and to explain any outliers. A commenter said they do not use Anthropic for serious work because normal work has been flagged for cyber security exploits many times. A commenter said they cannot imagine how to prove a negative and does not know if the poster is innocent.

A commenter said the situation shows how crazy things would be if the AI provider landscape settled into a monopoly or duopoly. A commenter said most people will be economically handicapped as a side effect of progress and that controlling the weights and means of inference will accumulate most of that value. A commenter said they were thinking shorter term, when AI still needs human babysitters for most knowledge work. A commenter said on a longer timeline everyone is in trouble without massive upheavals in socioeconomic systems.

The articles do not say what evidence the poster submitted or whether Anthropic responded. The articles do not say what happens to the account after the 24 hours. The articles do not give the company's name or Anthropic's statement on the case. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologizes to staff for violating company code of conduct
stories.Summary:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to employees on Tuesday for violating the company code of conduct. He spoke during his first all-hands meeting since returning to his role as chief executive. Huang stated that he made very serious personal mistakes which led to his resignation. He admitted that he hurt his wife and his family through these personal actions. The CEO also shared that he has been attending therapy every day for ninety minutes.

The board accepted his resignation earlier this month and reinstated him on Monday, eleven days later. This followed reports of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of ties to Chinese intelligence. The board acted after receiving fresh assurances and learning from the Trump administration he lacked federal scrutiny. Huang will now undergo a 360-degree performance review, soliciting feedback as often as every month. He claims he will be the first and only person at Nvidia to undergo this review.

Huang said this was the second hardest meeting he ever did, after a meeting with his wife. He stated that the company code of conduct, which he largely wrote, still governs employee treatment. He claimed that he needs to hold himself to a higher standard during this current time. Huang acknowledged that his intense management style sometimes disempowers employees and he takes things too far. He argued that his brief absence proved the company is wired to execute without him.

Some Nvidia employees celebrated the return of the CEO while others remain concerned about his personal conduct. One employee stated they would not do any more HR trainings if Huang returned to the company. Over 1,600 people commented on an internal post, with the majority supporting the decision to reinstall him. Women at the company are affected, though Huang described himself as one of their greatest advocates. He touted flexible work policies that allow employees to build their families and their careers simultaneously.

The board cited concerns about personal behavior and a lack of candor regarding his extramarital affairs. Huang began working with consultants from Heller in October 2025, when he was linked to a spy. The company opened an investigation into his affair with an alleged asset of Chinese intelligence services. Colette Kress, the chief financial officer, served as the interim CEO following his initial resignation on Thursday. The company has faced lawsuits and probes regarding its disclosures and compliance with US export controls.

The board is continuing an investigation into whether Huang was the target of foreign intelligence services. US lawmakers expect the CEO to testify before Congress during the coming week. Legal probes into Nvidia's compliance with chip export controls and its disclosures about behavior are still ongoing. The articles leave open whether Huang can maintain his dedication without hurting the people who work there. It remains unclear if the board will institute performance reviews for other employees beyond the CEO.

Articles.Title: In an all-hands, Jensen Huang apologized for violating Nvidia's code of conduct, saying he is in therapy after making "very serious personal mistakes" (Paresh Dave/Wired)

stories.Headline: Democratic governors in Texas, Ohio and Georgia vow to pause data center development
stories.Summary:
Newly elected Democratic governors in Texas, Ohio, and Georgia vowed to pause data center development in November 2026. Gina Hinojosa, Amy Acton, and Keisha Lance Bottoms are the officials who called for these moratoria. These leaders reacted after public opposition to artificial intelligence data centers reached a crescendo before the elections. Dozens of anti-data center initiatives passed nationwide during this period. The governors seek to halt approvals until new regulations are established.

Gina Hinojosa will impose a statewide moratorium in Texas until legislators pass guardrails for union hiring and water protection. These Texas rules would also give local communities the power to approve data center projects. In Georgia, Keisha Lance Bottoms plans to sign an executive order pausing development. Amy Acton was elected governor of Ohio and also called for a moratorium. These changes target the growth of AI infrastructure in these specific states.

Gina Hinojosa stated in a late October video that she will ban approvals to protect Texans. She believes the legislature must first pass laws regarding labor and resources. The governors claim that these pauses are necessary to address community impacts and infrastructure. They want to ensure that data centers do not harm local water resources. These officials are acting on the perceived needs of their constituents.

Many citizens expressed opposition to AI centers, fearing that such construction hikes electricity costs for average households. This public sentiment contributed to the success of various anti-data center initiatives across the country. The American Energy Alliance suggests that these policies could spell trouble for the future of American AI. Residents in Texas, Ohio, and Georgia are the primary people affected by these gubernatorial vows. These voters pushed the issue to the forefront of the election.

Texas currently ranks second only to Virginia in data centers due to cheap land and reliable energy. Bloom Energy projected that Texas would exceed 40 gigawatts of capacity by 2028. In September, Governor Greg Abbott had already ordered a pause on permits to audit projects for grid reliability. The articles state that Chinese operators used chatbots to create comic strips suggesting AI centers raise power costs. A bot farm of 200 China-linked accounts allegedly manipulated the debate on energy policy.

The U.S. Senate began discussing a bill on November 9 to make data center builders pay for their own power. This legislation would require these companies to invest in their local communities. The articles leave open whether the Democratic governors will successfully implement their moratoria. It remains unclear how these pauses will affect the global race for AI leadership. The final outcome of the Senate bill is also not yet determined.

Articles.Title: Newly Elected Democrats On AI Warpath - American Energy Alliance

stories.headline_source: Newly Elected Democrats On AI Warpath

stories.Headline: China Unicom launches Tongtong AI agent to provide personalized household services
stories.Summary:
China Unicom has developed the Tongtong agent as a core AI engine to empower household services for families across China. This technology powers four cloud-based products known as Unicom HomeMate, Unicom Cloud Disk, Unicom Cloud AI Phone, and Unicom Housekeeper. The system aims to bridge the digital divide for older adults, children, and busy middle-aged adults who face various everyday care challenges. By replacing complex remote controls with voice interaction, the agent provides accessible and human-centric AI experiences for millions of users.

The Tongtong agent supports the recognition of more than 200 Chinese dialects to help senior users operate devices through simple speech. It uses voiceprint and facial recognition to identify family members and provide personalized content recommendations on large screens. Multimodal visual recognition can detect indoor falls and immediately alert healthcare providers or family members to ensure safety. For children, the agent offers storytelling and guided exercises, while its AI-powered homework grading reaches an accuracy rate of over 90 percent. Middle-aged adults can use voice commands to draft work proposals, plan itineraries, or receive tailored fitness coaching in their living rooms.

China Unicom is responsible for these developments and claims that the Tongtong agent has already served 400 million household users. The company reports that these AI services have contributed hundreds of millions of US dollars in incremental revenue to the business. According to the company, it has shared its best practices with more than 10 operators worldwide to bring trustworthy AI to more families. The provider intends to continue enhancing the agent to extend its reach to people with disabilities and those living in remote areas.

Articles.Title: China Unicom empowers household AI services - China Daily Global Edition

stories.headline_source: China Unicom empowers household AI services

stories.Headline: Imperial College London hosts 48-hour biotech hackathon with Claude support for 120 builders
stories.Summary:
Imperial BioHack, an event brought by the Imperial College Computational Biology Society with the Entrepreneurship Society, is set to bring 120 interdisciplinary builders together at Imperial College in London for 48 hours of hacking, tentatively on 28 and 29 November at the City and Guilds Building. The gathering is supported by Claude, and its stated goal is for teams to leave with a working MVP, benchmark, pipeline, or even a preprint in under 48 hours. Teams will compete across three industry-led tracks set by biotech companies, with workshops, sponsor keynotes, and presentations rounding out the schedule. The listing says the venue and dates are tentative and subject to change, and that overnight hacking in the building is not expected to be permitted. Every participant is guaranteed $100 in Claude API credits, $200 in Cognition credits, Nebius compute credits, $250 in Amass platform credits per team, and a free ThinkCell subscription.

The three tracks and their prizes for the top three teams are Adaptyv Bio with £1k cash, $20k in Adaptyv platform credits, 100 designs validated in the lab, and $1k Claude credits, Helical Bio with £1.5k cash, a fast-track to an internship, Helical swag, Nebius credits, and $1k Claude credits, and Novogaia Bio with £1.5k cash, Nebius credits, and $1k Claude credits plus more to be confirmed. A £200 ThinkCell side challenge for best presentation is also up for grabs, and full prize and track details will be announced on the day of the hack. On Saturday registration opens at 9:00am, introduction and sponsor keynotes run from 10:00am to 11:15am, team formation and networking run from 11:15am to 12:00pm, hacking starts at 12:00pm, workshops run from 12:00pm to 2:00pm, and lunch and dinner follow, while on Sunday hacking ends at 12:00pm, judging and lunch run from 12:00pm to 1:30pm, presentations run from 2:00pm to 4:00pm, and awards follow from 4:00pm onwards. The event is organised by the Imperial College Computational Biology Society in collaboration with the Entrepreneurship Society, and the listing states that details come from the event listing and the organizer page, with registration managed by the organizer.

The listing advises people to confirm the venue with the organizer before traveling and to confirm current availability before making plans, and it says the organizer page was checked on 24 November 2026. It also notes that the exact schedule is to be determined, and that doors will be open to everyone on 29 November from 2pm onwards so people can see the projects and final presentations even if they are not hacking. The listing describes the event as an interdisciplinary platform for software engineers, biologists, statisticians, and anyone curious about hackathons or science to build solutions to real challenges set by biotech companies. stories.Headline: Carnival CEO Josh Weinstein says U.S. travel disruptions cost the company a few hundred million dollars in revenue
stories.Summary:
The second and final day of Center Stage at The Phocuswright Conference 2026 closed the event at the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, with sessions on who will sell travel once AI agents can book on a traveler's behalf, on the race to power banks, airlines and loyalty programs with travel technology, and on the policy pressures weighing on U.S. travel. Carnival Corporation President and CEO Josh Weinstein told U.S. Travel Association President and CEO Geoff Freeman that this year's disruptions have cost the company probably a few hundred million dollars in revenue, not counting fuel, and that the hit took a point or two off yields. Freeman described government shutdowns, hours-long TSA lines, air traffic controller shortages and a 25% drop in Canadian visitors as man-made problems, and said the U.S. will welcome around 12 million fewer international visitors than in 2019. Weinstein said tourism has a cabinet seat in every other major economy and should have one in the U.S., given it accounts for about 3% of GDP, and he said Princess Cruises was the first cruise brand to launch plugins for ChatGPT and Claude, a claim made by him. Booking Holdings is uniting its B2B operations into a single Booking Partner Division ahead of a January go-live, Agoda CEO Omri Morgenshtern told PhocusWire Executive Editor Linda Fox, and he said Priceline's B2B business is not part of the new division because of an ongoing FTC investigation.

Morgenshtern said he expects each major product line to be among the best in the world within six to 12 months, and that success will mean not losing partners to competitors on technology. Expedia Group is now launching B2B partners about 75% faster than before, and its new AI-powered front end has cut launch times from three or four months to three or four days, said Alfonso Paredes, President, B2B and Chief Commercial Officer, who also said agentic booking is overhyped in the short term but underhyped in the long term. Under an expanded partnership with Qantas, Expedia now powers the technology behind Qantas Holidays' own hotel contracts with chains such as Accor, Hilton and Marriott. Hopper CEO and co-founder Frederic Lalonde said Amex, Chase and Capital One sell around $30 billion of travel a year, a business growing about 22% annually compared with 4% to 6% for travel as a whole, and that Hopper's B2B platform HTS now connects to about 400 million cardholders in 23 countries, which he expects to double next year. He said Hopper did not sell itself to Capital One, which licensed its software and remains a customer, and he questioned whether travel marketplaces of any kind survive the shift to AI agents, saying blocking agents that act for customers is unlikely to work when more than half of internet traffic is no longer human.

In a session on who powers travel when AI becomes the seller, panelists Brett Burgess of ATPCO, Niklas Andréen of Sabre and Steve Domin of Duffel predicted AI agents could book anywhere from 15% to 50% of airline tickets within two years. Burgess suggested United's recent decision to stop AI agents booking its flights is likely linked to verifying who the buyer is, and an ATPCO study found AI agents answered questions about flight offers accurately only about 6% of the time, because fare rules and product details are often not machine-readable, while Domin said the booking itself already works smoothly and the harder work is handling changes and cancellations after booking. New Phocuswright research presented by Mike Coletta found that while 43% of U.S. travelers familiar with AI say they would book inside an AI platform, only 28% of travel companies are working or planning to become bookable there, and a survey of around 150 travel companies and start-ups found 45% are scaling or have scaled agentic AI, up from 28% in 2025, with start-ups further ahead than established companies. Companies that rebuilt core workflows around AI were more than twice as likely to report a major positive impact, at 92% versus 40%, and panelists said the technology to complete an agentic booking already exists but questions over who is accountable when something goes wrong are holding back volume.

Google Group Product Manager James Byers told Phocuswright's Mitra Sorrells that AI Overviews now reach 2.5 billion monthly users and AI Mode can take a traveler from research to a completed hotel booking, and that AI queries are three times longer than traditional searches, with one in five using voice or images. Meta's Sanjay Bhatia, Head of Industry, Travel and Auto, showed how brands can use Meta Business Agent and WhatsApp, now used by 100 million Americans each month, to handle bookings and service in a single conversation. Zerolook CEO Simone Lini showed an example in which an AI agent ran around 881,000 flight searches on Etihad's website, and the Zurich-based start-up, which predicts airfares without querying live systems and has raised $1.9 million, reported 96% pricing accuracy for one U.S. carrier. Pintours was named Travel Innovator of the Year at the Innovation Awards, with Groupize runner-up and ZentrumHub winning the audience-voted People's Choice award, and the conference featured 199 speakers across 42 sessions, with session recordings to be released over the coming weeks.

Articles.Title: B2B growth, AI booking and pressure on U.S. travel close The Phocuswright Conference 2026 - Hospitality Net

stories.Headline: Guelph officials use AI to find city efficiencies and improve services
stories.Summary:
City officials in Guelph are turning to artificial intelligence to find efficiencies, according to a presentation made at a Guelph Chamber of Commerce breakfast event on Tuesday, November 24, 2026. Chief Administrative Officer Tara Baker spoke at the event at the Victoria Park East Golf Club, where about 100 local business people attended along with several city staff and councillors. Baker was joined by deputy CAOs Colleen Clack-Bush, Terry Gayman and Stephen O'Brien, who each presented on the areas of city governance they oversee. The CAO's breakfast took the place of the chamber's annual municipal budget event because the 2027 budget update has not yet been presented due to last month's city election. According to the articles, the city is using AI to identify mis-sorted residential waste as it is collected by trucks, to track whether buses are on schedule and potentially to assess the grip of municipal equipment on wintry roads.

AI is also being used to assess infrastructure risks, model the repercussions of failures and plan how to lessen the impact or reduce the risk. Baker said the city is measuring its performance and how it does business, where it invests money, and is using those performance metrics to drive business decisions. O'Brien said part of the work includes breaking down departmental silos and removing redundant pages or information on the city's website, which he described as dated old legacy systems with highly siloed pockets of data and very low integration across platforms. Baker said the city is trying to improve those abilities through its focus on data management and business intelligence.

Clack-Bush said the city is focused on being efficient, finding ways to eliminate bureaucracy if it can and delivering services in a customer friendly way, noting the city is always looking at how technology can improve customer service. Gayman said the number one thing the city hears about is the housing need, along with transit, active transportation and the ability to provide options for people to get to work reliably. O'Brien said AI searches return a deeper analysis of results than a traditional Google search, making it all the more important that official city details are presented at the top of results pages, and that the city's data governance work matters because the business community needs confidence that the information it uses is accurate, timely and understood. Budget details are expected to be released in the new year, according to the articles.

Articles.Title: City hall turns to AI in attempt to improve efficiencies - Guelph News

stories.headline_source: City hall turns to AI in attempt to improve efficiencies

stories.Headline: Guterres tells Security Council killer robots must have no place in our future
stories.Summary:
The Security Council met on Tuesday to weigh how artificial intelligence and drones are reshaping warfare, with UN chief António Guterres telling ambassadors that killer robots must have no place in our future. The session examined how new technologies now spread globally within months rather than decades, and how disinformation is fuelling record levels of conflict. The council heard that artificial intelligence is already assisting in targeting and that drones are changing the way wars are fought. The meeting was held at UN headquarters and was carried live on UNWebTV. Guterres told council members they have a special duty to ensure that competition over emerging technologies does not destabilise international peace and security.

Last week in Geneva, a push by around 100 countries to negotiate a legally binding instrument on lethal autonomous weapons fell short. The Secretary-General's July review of UN peace operations made closing the technology gap a priority. A new informal council expert group on technology, peace and security met for the first time on 18 November, and in 2021 the council recognised technology as a potential force multiplier for UN peacekeeping. The Secretary-General is responsible for the July review of UN peace operations, which made closing the technology gap a priority, and he addressed the council directly on the duty of members. The council itself set up the informal expert group on technology, peace and security, which held its first meeting on 18 November.

The council also recognised technology in 2021 as a potential force multiplier for UN peacekeeping. Around 100 countries pushed in Geneva last week for a legally binding instrument on lethal autonomous weapons, but that effort fell short. The meeting comes as the UN marks more than eighty years since its founding in 1945, when computers, the internet and satellites were the stuff of science fiction. The articles do not say what the council will decide or when it will next take up the issue. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Security Council LIVE: Can conflict resolution keep pace as AI and drones reshape war? - UN News

stories.headline_source: Security Council LIVE: Can conflict resolution keep pace as AI and drones reshape war?

stories.Headline: Spartanburg Water CEO says AI posts mislead as utility reviews outage cause
stories.Summary:
Guy Boyle, the CEO of Spartanburg Water, spoke at a city county meeting on Monday, November 24, 2026. He explained a water outage that lasted several days and impacted residents across much of Spartanburg County. Boyle addressed AI social media posts, conversations about Duke Energy, and data center water usage. He stated that the exact cause of the power blip that led to the outage is still unknown.

The outage resulted from damage to a main 42-inch line and a secondary 24-inch line. Boyle noted that a brief power outage at the main plant may have lasted less than 10 seconds. The company is reviewing design weaknesses, valve analysis, surge relief systems, and additional levels of protection. He mentioned that the meter for NorthMark has not been ordered, installed, or connected yet.

Guy Boyle said that comments blaming Duke Energy for the damage were inaccurate and not communicated by Spartanburg Water. He described Duke Energy as a partner and stated that a post-mortem review of the infrastructure damage is underway. Boyle claimed that some residents shared misleading information to serve personal and political agendas. He stated that these conspiracy theories made the role of public service professionals more difficult.

Boyle acknowledged that social media comments regarding slow notification of the outage had merit. He explained that the current system cannot message all 276,000 customers simultaneously, so they used traditional and social media. Residents in Lyman and Woodruff had working ice machines because they are served by SJWD and WRWD. Boyle stated that these machines were left on so customers could have access to ice.

The company noted that some industry in the county was unaffected, including businesses in the Tiger River Industrial Park. Boyle cited Hurricane Helene as an example where infrastructure ran for two weeks without grid power. He stated that the systemwide boil water advisory was lifted on Sunday. The company told customers to call if they still experience air or cloudy water.

Spartanburg Water is currently working on a new notification system to better handle future systemwide events. The company and external electrical contractors are in the preliminary stages of investigating the power blip. The articles do not state when the new notification system will be fully operational. They do not provide a specific date for the completion of the infrastructure review. The final cause of the power blip remains undetermined.

stories.Headline: York County school board approves $107,100 for education software including AI platform MagicSchool
stories.Summary:
The York County School Board heard updates on a Spanish-language program, gifted education and artificial intelligence during its Tuesday meeting in Yorktown, according to Williamsburg Yorktown Daily. The Spanish program is a grant-funded pilot that operates at Bethel Manor Elementary School and Tabb Elementary School, which were chosen because they are the division's two schools with the most military-connected families. At Bethel Manor, students in kindergarten through fifth grade learn foundational Spanish language skills and explore Spanish culture in a world language resource class. Principal Anthony Friedman said students are building communication skills, curiosity and an appreciation for different perspectives that will help them in a changing world. A Bethel Manor student, Gabe Lugo, told the board he thinks other students should have the chance to learn Spanish because it helps people connect across different backgrounds.

The pilot depends on funding from a Department of Defense Education Activity grant, and Superintendent James Carroll said the division would be open to discussing expansion if the board wants the program in more schools. Carroll also said the division would consider local funding for the program. On gifted education, the board heard that more than 100 students are in the current referral cycle, and the Gifted Education Advisory Committee is reviewing the division's gifted education plan ahead of its 2027 expiration. The board unanimously approved October financial expenditures, Tabb High School additions and renovations totaling $38,100,000, and $107,100 for education software that includes the artificial intelligence platform MagicSchool and the digital learning platform ClassLink. Chief Academic Officer Candi Skinner said the division wants students prepared to use AI appropriately and responsibly in college or the work world, and she confirmed the AI program is monitored and has safeguards for student safety.

The board also reviewed a resolution on a policy called Equal Access to Public Education and Protection of Immigration and Citizenship-Related Information, which establishes that no student can be denied access to any division activity or benefit based on perceived immigration or citizenship status. The board approved consideration of a lease agreement between the school board and the Tabb Lakes Homes Association for the association to use school property for community meetings. The board's next meeting will be its Dec. 14 work session at 7 p.m. in York Hall.

Articles.Title: York school board hears updates on Spanish program, gifted education and AI - Williamsburg Yorktown Daily

stories.headline_source: York school board hears updates on Spanish program, gifted education and AI

stories.Headline: Chinese brands use AI micro dramas to reach consumers through narrative marketing
stories.Summary:
Brands in China are using AI micro dramas to engage consumers through artificial intelligence generated entertainment. Companies like FamilyMart and Pechoin produce these short stories to weave products into narratives. This marketing trend emerged as brands seek better ways to reach audiences than traditional ads. The shift allows commercial content to become part of the viewing experience for users. These productions use AI generated characters and settings to deliver brand messages.

The micro drama market exceeded 100 billion yuan in 2025, with 800 million users by September 2026. In the first eight months of 2026, 430,000 dramas were released, and AI productions accounted for 90 percent. FamilyMart created a series called Healing Moments at the Convenience Store focusing on work, communities, growth, romance, and school. Pechoin, founded in Shanghai in 1931, targets consumers aged 25 to 45 with fictional skincare stories. Taobao, Tmall, and Blue Moon launched an animated series featuring a magical creature from a body wash bottle.

Li Hao, the public relations director for FamilyMart, said AI dramas offer complete narratives for stores and services. He stated that products must appear when needed and membership benefits should help advance the plot. Wang Lujun, head of content marketing at Pechoin, said micro dramas reach larger audiences than conventional advertisements. She noted that AI allows the brand to create costly settings like polar regions. Executive producer Shen Chang said creators must balance storytelling, audience emotions, and commercial objectives.

Tang Jiansheng, a Shanghai based expert, said consumers are wary of direct pitches but receptive to chosen content. He noted that viewers may develop interest in products through storylines, which influences purchasing decisions. Consumers of skincare products are affected as brands move away from simply presenting ingredient data. Users of Hongguo Short Drama can pause videos to search for and order similar products via Douyin. The gap between high production volume and audience interest affects how brands approach content.

The National Radio and Television Administration provided data on the rapid growth of the micro drama market. An article from the China Netcasting Services Association noted live action dramas had more views during the Spring Festival. Pechoin noticed that traditional in feed advertisements on platforms like Douyin had reached a plateau in effectiveness. FamilyMart previously released two seasons of live action micro dramas before switching to AI technology. Hongguo Short Drama launched a creation program in October to match creators with brands.

FamilyMart plans to evaluate effectiveness by tracking viewing behavior, brand recognition, and new memberships across different regions. Brands may produce tailored versions of dramas for mothers, office workers, and older consumers in the future. AI could be used to analyze viewer comments to improve products, according to Tang Jiansheng. FamilyMart is exploring procedures for advertising disclosure, copyright protection, and the use of people's likenesses. The articles leave open how brands will maintain consumer trust amid excessive commercialization.

Articles.Title: Brands turn to AI micro dramas to engage consumers in China - Xinhua

stories.headline_source: Brands turn to AI micro dramas to engage consumers in China - Xinhua

stories.Headline: Analysts expect Singapore's economic growth to moderate in 2027 as the AI boom normalizes
stories.Summary:
Research houses reported on Tuesday, November 25, 2026, that Singapore's economic growth will likely moderate in 2027. This expected slowdown follows a period of strong expansion projected for the year 2026. Analysts believe that continued investment in infrastructure, semiconductor capacity, and artificial intelligence will provide necessary support. The general consensus suggests that the current boom in artificial intelligence will eventually normalize.

UOB Global Economics and Markets Research raised its 2026 growth forecast to 6.1 percent from 5.7 percent. This same firm upgraded its 2027 projection to 3.8 percent from 3.2 percent due to artificial intelligence tailwinds. Maybank Investment Bank Research also increased its 2026 forecast to 6.1 percent from 5.6 percent. Maybank further lifted its 2027 estimate to 4.2 percent from 3.3 percent, which sits near the top of the government range. The Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry projects a growth range between 2.5 percent and 4.5 percent for 2027.

DBS Group Research maintained its 2027 forecast at 3.5 percent while raising its 2026 estimate to 6.1 percent. DBS stated that global investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure will continue to rise but will move toward a more sustainable pace. The firm believes the cycle will shift from building infrastructure toward applications and adoption. This change comes as investors look closer at returns amid tighter financial conditions and new regulations. Maybank added that the ramp-up of VSMC's wafer plant and Micron's packaging facility should help the economy.

Maybank also noted that a robust pipeline of construction projects and energy infrastructure investments will support growth. These investments are part of a five-year plan managed by the Energy Market Authority. UOB warned that growth could slow in the second half of 2027 as hyperscaler spending decreases. Electronics exports and wholesale trade are expected to expand at a respectable but more moderate pace. The positive output gap is expected to narrow but remain sizeable according to UOB.

Articles.Title: Singapore's 2027 GDP growth seen moderating as AI boom normalizes - Xinhua

stories.headline_source: Singapore's 2027 GDP growth seen moderating as AI boom normalizes - Xinhua

stories.Headline: Malaysia tightens AI chip controls and discusses restrictions with the US
stories.Summary:
Malaysia is currently holding discussions with the United States regarding new restrictions on high-end artificial intelligence chip technology. The Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry is working with American officials to find common ground on these rules. These talks follow concerns that advanced Nvidia chips were being smuggled into China through various South-east Asian nations. Malaysia has pledged to comply with the regulations and is tightening its own internal controls to prevent future incidents.

The United States Commerce Department released an interim rule last week requiring licenses for advanced AI chip purchases. This requirement applies to data centre operators in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia to block adversaries from offshore computing power. The US has blacklisted several regional entities, including three that it claims are Malaysian, though Kuala Lumpur says only two are. Malaysia has instructed its data centre operators not to provide services or lease space to any of these blacklisted firms.

Second Finance Minister Amir Hamzah Azizan stated on November 25 that the country will comply with rules set by the relevant country. He downplayed the potential impact, noting that technology is used for cloud services and internal capacity beyond artificial intelligence. Amir clarified that Malaysia did not approve the shipments being questioned and is now taking steps to prevent similar occurrences. He believes that the demand for compute will continue to move forward despite these new regulatory challenges.

CIMB Bank warned in a November 19 report that Malaysia could lose the most in the region due to these curbs. The bank claims that GDP growth could be 0.19 percentage point lower in 2027 under a worst-case scenario. This scenario involves a six-month disruption to operations and a postponement of 25 percent of ongoing construction capacity. Malaysia previously reported RM123.5 billion in data centre and cloud investments during the first nine months of 2026.

Articles.Title: Malaysia talks with US on AI chip curbs, tightens controls - The Straits Times

stories.Headline: Myanmar worker pleads guilty to sending AI crocodile image that triggered Pandan Reservoir search
stories.Summary:
Ye Lin, a 30-year-old from Myanmar working in Singapore on a work permit, pleaded guilty to a charge of transmitting an image he knew to be false, after an AI-generated picture of a crocodile at Pandan Reservoir triggered search operations and the suspension of water activities. The court heard that on Aug 20 he was at the reservoir with a colleague when he took a photo of the water and said he had seen a crocodile, although there was none. He ran the photo through Gemini, a generative AI tool, inserted a crocodile into the image, and showed the modified photo to his colleague. Later he and other co-workers told a supervisor they had seen a crocodile, and the supervisor, shocked, asked for the photo, which Ye Lin sent to another colleague who forwarded it to the supervisor.

The supervisor immediately forwarded the image to a WhatsApp chat group with PUB officers, later saying he did so because the photograph looked real and it was very dangerous for the public to be around the waters if there really was a crocodile. PUB deployed an officer to check the sighting and informed the National Parks Board, which contracted a specialist to track the creature, while the Singapore Rowing Association and Singapore Canoe Federation were told to suspend all water activities at the reservoir. Checks were made with Ye Lin's colleague, who said he did not see the crocodile himself, and a check of Ye Lin's phone uncovered screenshots in the Gemini chat showing he had used the tool to fabricate the photo. When confronted he admitted there was no crocodile and that he had used AI to generate the picture, and a representative from PUB filed a police report stating that a PUB contractor had given false information about a crocodile sighting.

Ye Lin deleted the AI images and history records from the Gemini application on his phone, and after he was arrested he maintained at first that he had seen a real crocodile. He later said he had generated the image for his own amusement and did not know it would cause so much trouble, and a second charge of obstructing justice by deleting the AI-generated images will be considered in sentencing. Deputy Public Prosecutor Mavis Ng said several news agencies reached out to enquire about the crocodile and sought six to seven weeks' jail, saying Ye Lin had abused AI for no good reason except his own amusement, causing significant public alarm and leading government agencies to expend resources. She said that owing to his job he would have reasonably appreciated that the picture would have been sent at least to PUB.

Ye Lin was not represented by a lawyer and repeatedly confirmed he was not seeking legal representation, and he said through an interpreter that he truly regretted his actions and had not realised the impact they could have on government agencies and the public, including during the investigations. He looked anxious and fidgeted with his hands during his mitigation, added that he really wanted to continue working in Singapore and asked for a fine instead, and said he was the breadwinner for his mother, who is in Myanmar. He also said he had wanted to confess earlier but took a while to admit his mistake because he was too frightened and did not know what to do during investigations, and the judge adjourned sentencing to Dec 1. For transmitting an image he knew to be false, Ye Lin could be sentenced to up to three years' jail or fined up to S$10,000, or both, and CNA has reached out to PUB to ask whether he is still employed by its contractor.

Articles.Title: Man pleads guilty after AI-generated crocodile image sparks search at Pandan Reservoir - CNA

stories.Headline: Nvidia and Anthropic shares fall as AI stocks retreat and investors weigh new tariff risks
stories.Summary:
The Nasdaq and the S&P 500 closed lower on Tuesday as Nvidia and other AI-related shares gave back some of the previous day's sharp gains, while investors braced for possible new tariffs. Nvidia's stock slipped 5.9 percent as investors weighed the implications of Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO on Monday, following questions about the political and governance risks surrounding his return. Technology fell 2.8 percent, leading sector declines in the S&P 500, while an index of semiconductors dropped 7.9 percent. Nvidia's decision to bring back Huang drove a sharp rally in its stock and the market on Monday, giving the S&P 500 and Nasdaq their biggest daily percentage gains since April 2025. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 423.39 points, or 0.9 percent, to 50,018.70, the S&P 500 lost 36.08 points, or 0.5 percent, to 7,201.09 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 356.02 points, or 1.5 percent, to 23,733.54.

Reuters reported, citing three people with knowledge of the matter, that the Trump administration is poised to imminently release the findings of a probe aimed at countering alleged excess industrial capacity in 16 major US trading partners, and that new import duties on a wide range of goods are expected. Anthropic's shares ended 6.5 percent lower at US$81.90, below their US$83 IPO price, after the AI startup had a blockbuster market debut last week. Before Monday's rebound, AI-linked stocks had struggled for weeks as investors questioned the sector's debt-fuelled spending and the returns it could generate. Additional tariffs would add uncertainty to the market, while investors were also cautious ahead of Wednesday's Personal Consumption Expenditures report. Gene Goldman, chief investment officer at Cetera Financial Group, said that after the biggest rally in months you would expect some profit-taking, and that one headline does not really resolve investor questions about the AI trade.

He said the correction of last week is a buying opportunity for long-term investors, but that the path can be very bumpy for some time. The administration's tariffs have contributed to higher prices on consumer goods in the United States, and the PCE price index is one of the key inflation gauges watched by the Federal Reserve. Fed funds futures traders are pricing in 97 percent odds of a Fed hike in December, and a 66 percent chance of an additional increase in January, according to the CME Group's FedWatch Tool. Retailers were among the day's gainers, with shares of Abercrombie & Fitch jumping 19.7 percent after it raised its profit forecast, while Dollar Tree gained 11.2 percent, also after raising its profit outlook. Earlier, a Conference Board survey showed US consumer confidence rose to its highest level in nearly two years in November amid optimism over the labour market and the economy following this month's midterm elections.

stories.Headline: New Yorkers warned of holiday scams, AI shopping traps
stories.Summary:
New York Attorney General Letitia James issued a holiday scam warning on November 24, 2026, as reported by Long Island Business News. The warning tells New Yorkers to guard their personal information and to be careful when using artificial intelligence tools while shopping. James said she encourages holiday shoppers to protect themselves, their families and their private information by staying vigilant about potential scams. She also said no one should hesitate to report suspicious activity to her office. The warning covers receipts, buy now pay later loans, subscriptions, devices, phishing emails, fake deals, AI shopping tools and surveillance pricing.

James advised consumers to check that register prices match advertised or shelf prices. New York law requires retailers to charge the lowest advertised, posted or marked price and to keep at least 98% price accuracy during inspections by weights and measures officials. She said shoppers should review interest rates, payment schedules and fees on buy now, pay later loans before buying. Some of those loans charge interest even when payments are made on time, and missed payments may bring late fees and hurt credit scores. New York law requires businesses to clearly disclose subscription terms, obtain consent for automatic renewals, send post-purchase confirmation and offer an easy way to cancel.

James said consumers should update their home Wi-Fi password, avoid public Wi-Fi for purchases, install the latest software updates and keep antivirus software active. She warned that emails promoting exclusive holiday deals or free gift cards may be phishing attempts. She said shoppers should verify senders of unexpected holiday e-cards or invitations before clicking links or opening attachments. She advised shopping only on reputable websites, verifying URLs before entering payment information and checking for a working customer service number, a physical business address and positive customer reviews.

She said retailers that list only a P.O. box or have no working phone number deserve caution. James said shoppers should review all charges before purchasing because some websites add hefty delivery, processing or subscription fees, particularly during the holiday season. She said people using AI tools to make purchases should review what accounts and personal information the tool can access and limit permissions whenever possible. She said anyone whose AI tool can buy on their behalf should set clear spending limits and purchasing rules and require approval before purchases whenever possible.

New York's Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure Act requires most businesses that use personal data to set prices to display a clear disclosure near the price. Consumers who encounter undisclosed algorithmic pricing should file a complaint with the attorney general's office. James said shoppers should compare prices across retailers and platforms, use private or incognito browsing and check prices when logged out of loyalty accounts. She warned about inflated discounts and crossed-out prices and said shoppers should check price histories to judge whether a deal offers real savings.

She said consumers should keep order confirmations and receipts, contact the retailer if an item does not arrive as promised and file a complaint with her office if the company does not respond. She said people should review credit card and bank statements regularly for unauthorized charges, which may go unnoticed amid increased holiday spending. Suspected scam victims can report to the attorney general's office by submitting a complaint online or calling 1-800-771-7755. More to follow.

Articles.Title: New Yorkers warned of holiday scams, AI shopping traps - Long Island Business News

stories.Headline: India should test AI in regulatory sandboxes before deployment, speaker tells commerce summit
stories.Summary:
At the Indo-American Chamber of Commerce Summit in New Delhi last week, a speaker made five asks of the government on artificial intelligence, covering rules that work across India and America, trusted data flows, intellectual property protection, regulatory sandboxes and faster clearances for AI talent and data centres, and the sandbox drew the strongest response from the hall. The speaker described a sandbox as a learner's licence for a new technology and pointed to past practice, noting that UPI was launched on 11 April 2016 with 21 banks and grew under close watch of the existing payments law. In October this year, the speaker said, UPI handled 25.47 billion transactions in a single month, and in 2019 the Reserve Bank made the sandbox idea formal with a regulatory sandbox framework. In the latest round, five companies began testing and one product was found viable, and in 2025 an RBI committee recommended a sandbox for AI in finance with board-approved AI policies and the principle that whoever deploys AI answers for its decisions. The speaker said the government notified the Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam, 2026 this month, replacing aircraft rules written in 1937, with effect from January 2027, and called this the right moment to write an AI sandbox into them before any such system touches a passenger.

The speaker argued that a sandbox is also a legal instrument that provides rules for a limited time, to a limited audience and on strict conditions, and said every AI sandbox must answer five questions before the first test begins. On accountability, the speaker said the company that deploys should ideally be held accountable, while laws around the world are still being framed. On remedy, the speaker said a harmed customer must get a quick and certain remedy, with insurance or a compensation fund in place before testing starts. On data, the speaker said every test must comply with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act from the first day and that a sandbox must never relax privacy.

On honesty, the speaker said companies' admissions should not be used against them except in cases of fraud, and on endings, the speaker said every sandbox needs an exit plan before it begins. The speaker said these questions will soon reach the courts, giving the example of a bank refusing a loan or an airline holding a flight because an AI system said so, and noted that under Section 63 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam an electronic record needs a certificate before a court will admit it, so every sandbox should require AI decisions to be logged in a form a court can examine. The speaker said the legal profession must accept the same discipline, noting that more than five crore cases are pending in Indian courts and that courts and law firms are rightly testing AI for translation, research and document review, with an advocate sitting beside the machine and answering for every output. The speaker said the learner's mark comes off not because time has passed but because the driver has shown on real roads that he is ready, and urged giving AI in banking, aviation and law its learner's licence now.

stories.Headline: Xiaomi expands AI investment and focuses on MiMo model to recover costs
stories.Summary:
Xiaomi continues to increase its investment in artificial intelligence as of November 2026. The company released its third quarter financial report after the Hong Kong stock market closed on November 24. This report shows that the group is expanding its AI layout despite facing profit pressure. The company is focusing on the MiMo large model to achieve cost recovery. These investments are being integrated into mobile phone, automotive, and home scenarios.

The third quarter revenue reached 107.24 billion yuan, which is a 5.2 percent decrease year on year. Adjusted net profit fell 56.8 percent year on year to 4.88 billion yuan. Gross margin dropped to 20.2 percent from 22.9 percent in the same period last year. R&D expenditure for the first three quarters was 27.4 billion yuan, with AI exceeding 30 percent. New energy vehicle, AI, and innovative business revenue was 23.9 billion yuan in the third quarter.

Management stated that API calls for the MiMo large model and AI revenue continue to increase. The CFO noted that external revenue from these API calls has increased on a month on month basis. President Lu Weibing disclosed internal application progress and said he welcomes external B2B cooperation. The company claims the single-task cost of MiMo-V2.6-Pro is 1/20 to 1/60 of similar overseas models. These leaders believe the model can improve internal business and hardware sales.

The company is affected by rising costs of core components like storage and intensifying industry competition. Mobile phone shipments reached 30.7 million units, which is a 29.3 percent decrease year on year. Electric vehicle deliveries were 100,975 units, down 7.2 percent year on year. External customers are affected by the MiMo-V2.6-Pro overseas input price of 0.435 US dollars per million Tokens. Domestic customers pay 3 yuan for input and 6 yuan for output.

Xiaomi focused on end-side models before increasing investment in basic large models. Luo Fuli joined the MiMo team in November 2025 after working on DeepSeek-V2. The company released the MiMo-V2.6 series in September 2026. MiMo-V2.6-Pro scored about 46 points on the Artificial Analysis comprehensive intelligence index. The AIoT platform had 1.2035 billion connected devices and 771.9 million monthly active users by September 30.

Xiaomi is extending AI applications to factories and homes through robots and closed-loop agent systems. Robots completed 8-hour operation verification in automobile factories, and home agents started trial operation in youth apartments. The company has opened the weights of the MiMo-V2.6 series to attract developers. It remains open whether the robotics business has formed a mature and independent business model. The articles leave open if internal benefits can fully cover the large model investment.
